tools.name: PowerShell
tools.description:
Executes a given PowerShell command with optional timeout. Working directory persists between commands; shell state (variables, functions) does not.

IMPORTANT: This tool is for terminal operations via PowerShell: git, npm, docker, and PS cmdlets. DO NOT use it for file operations (reading, writing, editing, searching, finding files) - use the specialized tools for this instead.

PowerShell edition: Windows PowerShell 5.1 (powershell.exe)
   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.
   - Ternary (`?:`), null-coalescing (`??`), and null-conditional (`?.`) operators are NOT available. Use `if/else` and explicit `$null -eq` checks instead.
   - Avoid `2>&1` on native executables. In 5.1, redirecting a native command's stderr inside PowerShell wraps each line in an ErrorRecord (NativeCommandError) and sets `$?` to `$false` even when the exe returned exit code 0. stderr is already captured for you — don't redirect it.
   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.
   - `ConvertFrom-Json` returns a PSCustomObject, not a hashtable. `-AsHashtable` is not available.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:
   - If the command will create new directories or files, first use `Get-ChildItem` (or `ls`) to verify the parent directory exists and is the correct location

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required
   - 2>/dev/null → `2>$null` (but stderr is captured for you — usually unnecessary)
   - VAR=x cmd → `$env:VAR = 'x'; cmd` (PowerShell has no inline env-var prefix)
   - Bash control flow (`if [ -f x ]`, `for x in *`, backtick ``cmd`` substitution) is a parser error — use `if (Test-Path x)`, `foreach ($x in ...)`, `$(cmd)`

Exit-code note: `-ErrorAction SilentlyContinue` suppresses error OUTPUT but the cmdlet failure still causes this tool to report exit 1. To make a cmdlet failure truly non-fatal, promote it to terminating and swallow it: `try { Cmdlet ... -ErrorAction Stop } catch {}` (without `-ErrorAction Stop`, non-terminating errors skip the `catch` and still exit 1).

Interactive and blocking commands (this tool runs with -NonInteractive and stdin attached to the null device — console prompts read EOF or error immediately; GUI prompts can still block until timeout):
   - NEVER use `Read-Host`, `Get-Credential`, `Out-GridView`, `$Host.UI.PromptForChoice`, or `pause`
   - Destructive cmdlets (`Remove-Item`, `Stop-Process`, `Clear-Content`, etc.) may prompt for confirmation. Add `-Confirm:$false` when you intend the action to proceed. Use `-Force` for read-only/hidden items.
   - Never use `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`, or other commands that open an interactive editor

Passing multiline strings (commit messages, file content) to native executables:
   - Use a single-quoted here-string so PowerShell does not expand `$` or backticks inside. The closing `'@` MUST be at column 0 (no leading whitespace) on its own line — indenting it is a parse error:
<example>
git commit -m @'
Commit message here.
Second line with $literal dollar signs.
'@
</example>
   - Use `@'...'@` (single-quoted, literal) not `@"..."@` (double-quoted, interpolated) unless you need variable expansion
   - For arguments containing `-`, `@`, or other characters PowerShell parses as operators, use the stop-parsing token: `git log --% --format=%H`

Usage notes:
  - The command argument is required.
  - You can specify an optional timeout in milliseconds (up to 600000ms / 10 minutes for a foreground command). If not specified, commands will timeout after 120000ms (2 minutes).
  - It is very helpful if you write a clear, concise description of what this command does.
  - If the output exceeds 30000 characters, output will be truncated before being returned to you.
  - You can use the `run_in_background` parameter to run the command in the background. Only use this if you don't need the result immediately and are OK being notified when the command completes later. You do not need to check the output right away - you'll be notified when it finishes.
  - Avoid using PowerShell to run commands that have dedicated tools, unless explicitly instructed:
    - File search: Use Glob (NOT Get-ChildItem -Recurse)
    - Content search: Use Grep (NOT Select-String)
    - Read files: Use Read (NOT Get-Content)
    - Edit files: Use Edit
    - Write files: Use Write (NOT Set-Content/Out-File)
    - Communication: Output text directly (NOT Write-Output/Write-Host)
  - When issuing multiple commands:
    - If the commands are independent and can run in parallel, make multiple PowerShell tool calls in a single message.
    - If the commands depend on each other and must run sequentially, chain them in a single PowerShell call (see edition-specific chaining syntax above).
    - Use `;` only when you need to run commands sequentially but don't care if earlier commands fail.
    - DO NOT use newlines to separate commands (newlines are ok in quoted strings and here-strings)
  - Do NOT prefix commands with `cd` or `Set-Location` -- the working directory is already set to the correct project directory automatically.
  - Avoid unnecessary `Start-Sleep` commands:
    - Do not sleep between commands that can run immediately — just run them.
    - If your command is long running and you would like to be notified when it finishes — simply run your command using `run_in_background`. There is no need to sleep in this case.
    - Do not retry failing commands in a sleep loop — diagnose the root cause or consider an alternative approach.
    - If waiting for a background task you started with `run_in_background`, you will be notified when it completes — do not poll.
    - If you must poll an external process, use a check command rather than sleeping first.
    - If you must sleep, keep the duration short to avoid blocking the user.
  - For git commands:
    - Prefer to create a new commit rather than amending an existing commit.
    - Before running destructive operations (e.g., git reset --hard, git push --force, git checkout --), consider whether there is a safer alternative that achieves the same goal. Only use destructive operations when they are truly the best approach.
    - Never skip hooks (--no-verify) or bypass signing (--no-gpg-sign, -c commit.gpgsign=false) unless the user has explicitly asked for it. If a hook fails, investigate and fix the underlying issue.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

For this vulnerability specifically, four W01 Domain Controllers with Windows Server 2022, running AD DS, DNS, Kerberos and Group Policy, in the IDENTITY zone (10.20.20.0/24 at HQ and 10.40.x.0/24 at recovery-site overlay). 20	[List Paragraph] Evidence and Uncertainty: Provide source references, locators, dates, retrieval date, and live or cached status for each fact. Assumptions and unknowns should be explicitly called out. Explained confidence rating of high if all factors are cited to a source, medium if there are assumptions used in any of the scoring / applicability or any tool calls failed, and low if a decisive fact is unknown or a required lookup failed.

1	"""Northbridge rating policy (rating-policy-v1.0).
2	
3	Deterministic implementation of the group's applicability-and-impact policy.
4	The model gathers facts with tools and records its judgments (condition
5	results, reachability, criticality, blast radius). This module turns those
6	facts into scores, a rating and a policy rule. The model never picks the
7	rating itself.
8	
9	Gate 1 - Applicability (C1 affected OS, C2 DNS Server installed, C3 build
10	below fixed build). Precedence when several outcomes are possible:
11	    1. any condition "false"       -> P-NA  (Low, Not Applicable)
12	    2. decisive tool failure       -> P-RV-F (Review Needed)
13	    3. any condition "conflicting" -> P-RV-C (Review Needed)
14	    4. any condition "unknown"     -> P-IE  (Insufficient Evidence)
15	    5. all "true"                  -> Gate 2
16	A confirmed "false" wins because one missing prerequisite is enough to show
17	the vulnerability is not present. The design doc lists the outcomes but not
18	their precedence; this order is the group's choice.
19	
20	Gate 2 - Likelihood (sum, 0-6) x Impact (max, 0-2) -> rating matrix.
21	When Gate 1 ends in P-IE and Gate 2 inputs are available, Gate 2 is also
22	computed as a non-binding provisional rating for prioritization.
23	"""
24	
25	from __future__ import annotations
26	
27	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
28	from typing import Optional
29	
30	POLICY_VERSION = "rating-policy-v1.0"
31	
32	CONDITION_VALUES = {"true", "false", "unknown", "conflicting"}
33	LEVEL_CODE = {"Low": "L", "Medium": "M", "High": "H"}
34	IMPACT_LEVELS = ["Low", "Medium", "High"]
35	
36	# Rows: likelihood level, columns: impact level.
37	MATRIX = {
38	    "Low": {"Low": "Low", "Medium": "Low", "High": "Medium"},
39	    "Medium": {"Low": "Low", "Medium": "Medium", "High": "High"},
40	    "High": {"Low": "Medium", "Medium": "High", "High": "High"},
41	}
42	
43	
44	@dataclass
45	class PolicyInputs:
46	    """Facts the agent gathered. None means unknown."""
47	
48	    conditions: dict[str, str]                  # {"C1": "true", "C2": "true", "C3": "unknown"}
49	    decisive_tool_failure: bool = False         # lookup_vulnerability or environment_search failed, no cache
50	
51	    # Likelihood
52	    reachability: Optional[int] = None          # 0 isolated, 1 broad internal, 2 Internet-facing; None -> default 1
53	    cvss_metrics: Optional[dict[str, str]] = None  # {"AV": "N", "AC": "L", "PR": "N", "UI": "N", "C": "H", "I": "H", "A": "H"}
54	    kev_listed: Optional[bool] = None
55	    credible_in_the_wild: Optional[bool] = None
56	    public_poc: Optional[bool] = None
57	    vendor_exploitation_likely: Optional[bool] = None
58	
59	    # Impact
60	    asset_criticality: Optional[int] = None     # 0 non-critical, 1 business-important, 2 critical
61	    blast_radius: Optional[int] = None          # 0 single host, 1 service/department, 2 domain/organization
62	    rto_hours: Optional[float] = None
63	
64	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
65	        for cid, val in self.conditions.items():
66	            if val not in CONDITION_VALUES:
67	                raise ValueError(f"{cid}: '{val}' is not one of {sorted(CONDITION_VALUES)}")
68	        for name in ("reachability", "asset_criticality", "blast_radius"):
69	            val = getattr(self, name)
70	            if val is not None and val not in (0, 1, 2):
71	                raise ValueError(f"{name} must be 0, 1, 2 or None, got {val!r}")
72	
73	
74	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Gate 1
75	
76	def gate_1(inp: PolicyInputs) -> tuple[str, str]:
77	    """Return (applicability_status, gate_1_outcome)."""
78	    values = set(inp.conditions.values())
79	    if "false" in values:
80	        return "Not Applicable", "P-NA"
81	    if inp.decisive_tool_failure:
82	        return "Unknown", "P-RV-F"
83	    if "conflicting" in values:
84	        return "Conflicting", "P-RV-C"
85	    if "unknown" in values:
86	        return "Unknown", "P-IE"
87	    return "Confirmed", "Gate 2"
88	
89	
90	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Gate 2
91	
92	def exploitability_score(m: dict[str, str]) -> int:
93	    if m.get("AV") in ("L", "P"):
94	        return 0
95	    if m.get("AV") in ("N", "A") and m.get("AC") == "L" and m.get("PR") == "N" and m.get("UI") == "N":
96	        return 2
97	    if m.get("AV") in ("N", "A"):
98	        return 1
99	    raise ValueError(f"Cannot score exploitability from CVSS metrics {m}")
100	
101	
102	def exploit_activity_score(inp: PolicyInputs) -> int:
103	    if inp.kev_listed or inp.credible_in_the_wild:
104	        return 2
105	    if inp.public_poc or inp.vendor_exploitation_likely:
106	        return 1
107	    return 0
108	
109	
110	def likelihood_level(score: int) -> str:
111	    return "Low" if score <= 2 else "Medium" if score <= 4 else "High"
112	
113	
114	def gate_2_available(inp: PolicyInputs) -> bool:
115	    return inp.cvss_metrics is not None and inp.asset_criticality is not None and inp.blast_radius is not None
116	
117	
118	def likelihood(inp: PolicyInputs) -> dict:
119	    defaulted = inp.reachability is None
120	    reach = 1 if defaulted else inp.reachability
121	    expl = exploitability_score(inp.cvss_metrics)
122	    act = exploit_activity_score(inp)
123	    raw = reach + expl + act
124	    cap = reach == 0
125	    final = min(raw, 1) if cap else raw
126	    return {
127	        "factors": {
128	            "reachability": {"score": reach, "defaulted": defaulted},
129	            "exploitability": {"score": expl},
130	            "exploit_activity": {"score": act},
131	        },
132	        "raw_sum": raw,
133	        "reachability_cap_applied": cap,
134	        "final_score": final,
135	        "level": likelihood_level(final),
136	    }
137	
138	
139	def _clamp(x: int) -> int:
140	    return max(0, min(2, x))
141	
142	
143	def impact(inp: PolicyInputs) -> dict:
144	    base = max(inp.asset_criticality, inp.blast_radius)
145	    m = inp.cvss_metrics
146	
147	    rto_known = inp.rto_hours is not None
148	    rto_trig = rto_known and inp.rto_hours <= 4
149	    cia_trig = all(m.get(k) in ("L", "N") for k in ("C", "I", "A"))
150	    effects = {"ADJ-RTO": 1 if rto_trig else 0, "ADJ-CIA": -1 if cia_trig else 0}
151	
152	    final = _clamp(base + sum(effects.values()))
153	    adjustments = []
154	    for adj_id, triggered, status, value in (
155	        ("ADJ-RTO", rto_trig, "known" if rto_known else "unknown", inp.rto_hours),
156	        ("ADJ-CIA", cia_trig, "known", f"C:{m.get('C')}/I:{m.get('I')}/A:{m.get('A')}"),
157	    ):
158	        without = _clamp(base + sum(v for k, v in effects.items() if k != adj_id))
159	        adjustments.append({
160	            "id": adj_id,
161	            "input_value": value,
162	            "input_status": status,
163	            "triggered": triggered,
164	            "effect": effects[adj_id],
165	            "binding": without != final,
166	        })
167	    return {
168	        "factors": {
169	            "asset_criticality": {"score": inp.asset_criticality},
170	            "blast_radius": {"score": inp.blast_radius},
171	        },
172	        "base_score": base,
173	        "adjustments": adjustments,
174	        "final_score": final,
175	        "level": IMPACT_LEVELS[final],
176	    }
177	
178	
179	def matrix(lk: dict, im: dict) -> dict:
180	    rating = MATRIX[lk["level"]][im["level"]]
181	    return {
182	        "likelihood_level": lk["level"],
183	        "impact_level": im["level"],
184	        "rating": rating,
185	        "policy_rule": f"P-{LEVEL_CODE[rating]}-L{lk['final_score']}I{im['final_score']}",
186	    }
187	
188	
189	# ---------------------------------------------------------------- Entry point
190	
191	def evaluate(inp: PolicyInputs) -> dict:
192	    """Apply the full policy. Returns the decision and the scored rationale blocks."""
193	    status, outcome = gate_1(inp)
194	
195	    lk = im = mx = None
196	    if outcome in ("Gate 2", "P-IE") and gate_2_available(inp):
197	        lk, im = likelihood(inp), impact(inp)
198	        mx = matrix(lk, im)
199	    elif outcome == "Gate 2":
200	        raise ValueError("Applicability confirmed but Gate 2 inputs (CVSS metrics, criticality, blast radius) are missing")
201	
202	    if outcome == "Gate 2":
203	        decision = {"rating": mx["rating"], "policy_rule_applied": mx["policy_rule"], "gate_reached": "Gate 2", "provisional": None}
204	        gate_2_status = "evaluated"
205	    else:
206	        rating = {"P-NA": "Low", "P-IE": "Insufficient Evidence"}.get(outcome, "Review Needed")
207	        provisional = None
208	        if outcome == "P-IE" and mx:
209	            provisional = {"rating": mx["rating"], "policy_rule": mx["policy_rule"], "binding": False}
210	        decision = {"rating": rating, "policy_rule_applied": outcome, "gate_reached": "Gate 1", "provisional": provisional}
211	        gate_2_status = "provisional" if provisional else "not_evaluated"
212	        if not provisional:
213	            lk = im = mx = None
214	
215	    return {
216	        "policy_version": POLICY_VERSION,
217	        "decision": decision,
218	        "applicability": {"status": status, "gate_1_outcome": outcome},
219	        "gate_2_status": gate_2_status,
220	        "likelihood": lk,
221	        "impact": im,
222	        "matrix_result": mx,
223	    }
224	
225	
226	def parse_cvss_vector(vector: str) -> dict[str, str]:
227	    """'CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/...' -> {'AV': 'N', 'AC': 'L', ...}"""
228	    parts = [p.split(":", 1) for p in vector.split("/") if ":" in p]
229	    return {k: v for k, v in parts if k != "CVSS"}
230

1	"""Validate an assessment JSON.
2	
3	1. Structure: JSON Schema (assessment_schema.json) - fields, types, allowed values.
4	2. Consistency: cross-field rules the schema does not express - evidence references,
5	   source labeling, tool-contract rules, and agreement with policy.py.
6	
7	Usage:
8	    python validate.py assessment.json [--schema assessment_schema.json] [--write]
9	
10	--write stores the check results in the assessment's "validation" block.
11	Exit code 0 when every check passes, 1 otherwise.
12	"""
13	
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	import argparse
17	import json
18	import re
19	import sys
20	from pathlib import Path
21	
22	import jsonschema
23	
24	from policy import PolicyInputs, evaluate, parse_cvss_vector
25	
26	HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
27	DEFAULT_SCHEMA = HERE / "assessment_schema.json"
28	
29	ENV_QUERY_TYPES = {"asset", "text", "flows", "business_service"}
30	CVE_RE = re.compile(r"^CVE-\d{4}-\d{4,}$")
31	EVIDENCE_ID_RE = re.compile(r'"(E\d+)"')
32	DECISIVE_TOOLS = {"lookup_vulnerability", "environment_search"}
33	
34	
35	def _check(results: list, name: str, problems: list[str]) -> None:
36	    results.append({"check": name, "passed": not problems, "detail": "; ".join(problems) or "ok"})
37	
38	
39	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ structure
40	
41	def check_schema(a: dict, schema: dict) -> list[str]:
42	    v = jsonschema.Draft202012Validator(schema)
43	    return [f"{'/'.join(map(str, e.absolute_path)) or '(root)'}: {e.message}" for e in v.iter_errors(a)]
44	
45	
46	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ references
47	
48	def check_evidence_refs(a: dict) -> list[str]:
49	    ids = [e["evidence_id"] for e in a.get("evidence", [])]
50	    problems = [f"duplicate evidence_id {i}" for i in set(ids) if ids.count(i) > 1]
51	    body = json.dumps({k: v for k, v in a.items() if k not in ("evidence", "validation")})
52	    cited = set(EVIDENCE_ID_RE.findall(body))
53	    problems += [f"{i} cited but not in evidence[]" for i in sorted(cited - set(ids))]
54	    problems += [f"{i} in evidence[] but never cited" for i in sorted(set(ids) - cited)]
55	    return problems
56	
57	
58	def check_tool_refs(a: dict) -> list[str]:
59	    calls = {t["call_id"] for t in a.get("tool_trace", [])}
60	    return [f"{e['evidence_id']} points to unknown tool call {e['tool_call_id']}"
61	            for e in a.get("evidence", []) if e.get("tool_call_id") not in calls]
62	
63	
64	def check_unknown_refs(a: dict) -> list[str]:
65	    unknowns = {u["id"]: u for u in a.get("unknowns", [])}
66	    problems = []
67	    for uid in a["decision"].get("missing_decisive_facts") or []:
68	        if uid not in unknowns:
69	            problems.append(f"missing_decisive_facts lists {uid}, which is not in unknowns[]")
70	        elif not unknowns[uid]["decisive"]:
71	            problems.append(f"{uid} is listed as a missing decisive fact but unknowns[].decisive is false")
72	    if a["decision"]["policy_rule_applied"] == "P-IE" and not a["decision"].get("missing_decisive_facts"):
73	        problems.append("P-IE requires at least one entry in missing_decisive_facts")
74	    return problems
75	
76	
77	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ labeling
78	
79	def check_labels(a: dict) -> list[str]:
80	    problems = []
81	    for e in a.get("evidence", []):
82	        if e["retrieval_mode"] == "cached" and not e.get("fallback_reason"):
83	            problems.append(f"{e['evidence_id']} is cached but has no fallback_reason")
84	        if e["source_type"] == "environment_snapshot" and e["retrieval_mode"] != "simulated":
85	            problems.append(f"{e['evidence_id']} comes from the environment but is not labeled simulated")
86	    return problems
87	
88	
89	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ tool contracts
90	
91	def check_tool_contracts(a: dict) -> list[str]:
92	    problems = []
93	    invalid_counts: dict[str, int] = {}
94	    for t in a.get("tool_trace", []):
95	        cid, tool, args, status = t["call_id"], t["tool"], t["arguments"], t["result_status"]
96	        if status in ("failed", "invalid_request") and not t.get("error"):
97	            problems.append(f"{cid}: {status} without an error message")
98	        if status == "invalid_request":
99	            invalid_counts[tool] = invalid_counts.get(tool, 0) + 1
100	            if t["evidence_ids"]:
101	                problems.append(f"{cid}: an invalid request cannot produce evidence")
102	            continue
103	        if tool == "environment_search":
104	            if args.get("query_type") not in ENV_QUERY_TYPES:
105	                problems.append(f"{cid}: query_type must be one of {sorted(ENV_QUERY_TYPES)}")
106	            if not args.get("query"):
107	                problems.append(f"{cid}: environment_search requires a non-empty query")
108	            if t["mode"] not in ("simulated", None):
109	                problems.append(f"{cid}: environment_search mode must be simulated")
110	        elif tool == "tavily_search":
111	            for k in ("query", "allowed_domains", "max_results"):
112	                if k not in args:
113	                    problems.append(f"{cid}: tavily_search missing argument {k}")
114	            if t["mode"] not in ("live", None) or t["fallback_used"]:
115	                problems.append(f"{cid}: tavily_search is live only with no fallback")
116	        elif tool in ("lookup_kev", "lookup_vulnerability"):
117	            if not CVE_RE.match(str(args.get("cve_id", ""))):
118	                problems.append(f"{cid}: invalid cve_id {args.get('cve_id')!r}")
119	    for tool, n in invalid_counts.items():
120	        if n > 1:
121	            problems.append(f"{tool}: {n} invalid requests; only one correction attempt is allowed")
122	    return problems
123	
124	
125	def check_kev_matches_tool(a: dict) -> list[str]:
126	    lk = a["rationale"].get("likelihood")
127	    if not lk:
128	        return []
129	    recorded = lk["factors"]["exploit_activity"]["kev_listed"]
130	    kev_calls = [t for t in a["tool_trace"] if t["tool"] == "lookup_kev" and t["result_status"] in ("found", "not_found")]
131	    if not kev_calls:
132	        return [] if recorded is None else ["kev_listed is set but no successful lookup_kev call exists"]
133	    expected = kev_calls[-1]["result_status"] == "found"
134	    return [] if recorded == expected else [f"kev_listed is {recorded} but lookup_kev returned {kev_calls[-1]['result_status']}"]
135	
136	
137	def check_conflicts(a: dict) -> list[str]:
138	    if a["decision"]["policy_rule_applied"] == "P-RV-C" and not a.get("conflicts"):
139	        return ["P-RV-C requires at least one entry in conflicts[]"]
140	    return []
141	
142	
143	def check_cvss_consistency(a: dict) -> list[str]:
144	    lk = a["rationale"].get("likelihood")
145	    vector = a["severity_vs_local_risk"]["technical_severity"].get("vector")
146	    if not lk or not vector:
147	        return []
148	    m = parse_cvss_vector(vector)
149	    ex = lk["factors"]["exploitability"]
150	    return [f"exploitability.cvss_{k.lower()} is {ex.get('cvss_' + k.lower())} but vector has {m.get(k)}"
151	            for k in ("AV", "AC", "PR", "UI") if ex.get("cvss_" + k.lower()) != m.get(k)]
152	
153	
154	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ policy
155	
156	def inputs_from_assessment(a: dict) -> PolicyInputs:
157	    """Rebuild the policy inputs from what the assessment recorded."""
158	    r = a["rationale"]
159	    vector = a["severity_vs_local_risk"]["technical_severity"].get("vector")
160	    kw = dict(
161	        conditions={c["id"]: c["result"] for c in r["applicability"]["conditions"]},
162	        decisive_tool_failure=any(t["tool"] in DECISIVE_TOOLS and t["result_status"] == "failed" for t in a["tool_trace"]),
163	        cvss_metrics=parse_cvss_vector(vector) if vector else None,
164	    )
165	    if r.get("likelihood"):
166	        f = r["likelihood"]["factors"]
167	        reach = f["reachability"]
168	        ea = f["exploit_activity"]
169	        kw.update(
170	            reachability=None if reach["defaulted"] else reach["score"],
171	            kev_listed=ea["kev_listed"],
172	            credible_in_the_wild=ea["credible_in_the_wild"],
173	            public_poc=ea["public_poc"],
174	            vendor_exploitation_likely=ea["vendor_exploitation_likely"],
175	        )
176	    if r.get("impact"):
177	        f = r["impact"]["factors"]
178	        rto = next((x for x in r["impact"]["adjustments"] if x["id"] == "ADJ-RTO"), None)
179	        kw.update(
180	            asset_criticality=f["asset_criticality"]["score"],
181	            blast_radius=f["blast_radius"]["score"],
182	            rto_hours=rto["input_value"] if rto and rto["input_status"] == "known" else None,
183	        )
184	    return PolicyInputs(**kw)
185	
186	
187	def _diff(path: str, expected, actual, out: list[str]) -> None:
188	    if expected != actual:
189	        out.append(f"{path}: policy gives {expected!r}, assessment has {actual!r}")
190	
191	
192	def check_policy(a: dict) -> list[str]:
193	    try:
194	        exp = evaluate(inputs_from_assessment(a))
195	    except (ValueError, KeyError, TypeError) as err:
196	        return [f"policy could not be applied: {err}"]
197	    r, d, out = a["rationale"], a["decision"], []
198	
199	    for k in ("rating", "policy_rule_applied", "gate_reached"):
200	        _diff(f"decision.{k}", exp["decision"][k], d[k], out)
201	    prov = d.get("provisional")
202	    _diff("decision.provisional", exp["decision"]["provisional"],
203	          {k: prov[k] for k in ("rating", "policy_rule", "binding")} if prov else None, out)
204	    for k in ("status", "gate_1_outcome"):
205	        _diff(f"applicability.{k}", exp["applicability"][k], r["applicability"][k], out)
206	    _diff("gate_2_status", exp["gate_2_status"], r["gate_2_status"], out)
207	
208	    for block in ("likelihood", "impact", "matrix_result"):
209	        e, got = exp[block], r.get(block)
210	        if (e is None) != (got is None):
211	            out.append(f"{block}: policy gives {'null' if e is None else 'a value'}, assessment has {'null' if got is None else 'a value'}")
212	            continue
213	        if e is None:
214	            continue
215	        if block == "matrix_result":
216	            for k, v in e.items():
217	                _diff(f"matrix_result.{k}", v, got[k], out)
218	            continue
219	        for fname, fexp in e["factors"].items():
220	            for k, v in fexp.items():
221	                _diff(f"{block}.factors.{fname}.{k}", v, got["factors"][fname][k], out)
222	        for k in e:
223	            if k not in ("factors", "adjustments"):
224	                _diff(f"{block}.{k}", e[k], got[k], out)
225	        if block == "impact":
226	            got_adj = {x["id"]: x for x in got["adjustments"]}
227	            for adj in e["adjustments"]:
228	                g = got_adj.get(adj["id"])
229	                if not g:
230	                    out.append(f"impact.adjustments: {adj['id']} missing")
231	                    continue
232	                for k in ("triggered", "effect", "binding", "input_status"):
233	                    _diff(f"impact.adjustments[{adj['id']}].{k}", adj[k], g[k], out)
234	    return out
235	
236	
237	# ------------------------------------------------------------------ entry point
238	
239	def validate_assessment(a: dict, schema: dict) -> dict:
240	    results: list = []
241	    schema_problems = check_schema(a, schema)
242	    _check(results, "Output matches assessment_schema.json", schema_problems)
243	    if schema_problems:  # later checks assume a well-formed document
244	        return {"schema_valid": False, "checks": results}
245	    _check(results, "Every cited evidence_id exists and every evidence item is cited", check_evidence_refs(a))
246	    _check(results, "Every evidence item points to a call in tool_trace", check_tool_refs(a))
247	    _check(results, "Missing decisive facts are listed in unknowns[]", check_unknown_refs(a))
248	    _check(results, "Cached evidence has a fallback reason; environment evidence is labeled simulated", check_labels(a))
249	    _check(results, "Tool calls follow the tool contracts", check_tool_contracts(a))
250	    _check(results, "kev_listed matches the lookup_kev result", check_kev_matches_tool(a))
251	    _check(results, "Exploitability CVSS fields match the CVSS vector", check_cvss_consistency(a))
252	    _check(results, "Review Needed for conflicting evidence lists the conflicts", check_conflicts(a))
253	    _check(results, "Decision, scores and matrix match policy.py", check_policy(a))
254	    return {"schema_valid": True, "checks": results}
255	
256	
257	def main() -> int:
258	    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
259	    ap.add_argument("assessment", type=Path)
260	    ap.add_argument("--schema", type=Path, default=DEFAULT_SCHEMA)
261	    ap.add_argument("--write", action="store_true", help="store results in the assessment's validation block")
262	    args = ap.parse_args()
263	
264	    a = json.loads(args.assessment.read_text())
265	    report = validate_assessment(a, json.loads(args.schema.read_text()))
266	    for c in report["checks"]:
267	        print(f"[{'PASS' if c['passed'] else 'FAIL'}] {c['check']}" + ("" if c["passed"] else f"\n       {c['detail']}"))
268	    if args.write:
269	        a["validation"] = report
270	        args.assessment.write_text(json.dumps(a, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
271	    return 0 if all(c["passed"] for c in report["checks"]) else 1
272	
273	
274	if __name__ == "__main__":
275	    sys.exit(main())

1	"""Policy tests. The first four map to the Assignment 2 policy checks.
2

Executive SummaryUse after free in Windows DNS allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.
Metrics
CVSS:3.1 9.8 / 8.5 Base score metrics: 9.8 / Temporal score metrics: 8.5
Expand all Collapse all
Metric Value
Base score metrics (8)
Attack Vector
This metric reflects the context by which vulnerability
exploitation is possible. The Base Score increases the more
remote (logically, and physically) an attacker can be in order to
exploit the vulnerable component.
Network
The vulnerable component is bound to the network stack and the set of possible attackers extends beyond the other options listed, up to and
including the entire Internet. Such a vulnerability is often termed 'remotely exploitable' and can be thought of as an attack being exploitable at
the protocol level one or more network hops away (e.g., across one or more routers).
Attack Complexity
This metric describes the conditions beyond the attacker’s
control that must exist in order to exploit the vulnerability. Such
conditions may require the collection of more information
about the target or computational exceptions. The assessment
of this metric excludes any requirements for user interaction in
order to exploit the vulnerability. If a specific configuration is
required for an attack to succeed, the Base metrics should be
scored assuming the vulnerable component is in that
configuration.
Low
Specialized access conditions or extenuating circumstances do not exist. An attacker can expect repeatable success against the vulnerable
component.
Privileges Required
This metric describes the level of privileges an attacker must
possess before successfully exploiting the vulnerability.
None
The attacker is unauthorized prior to attack, and therefore does not require any access to settings or files to carry out an attack.
User Interaction
This metric captures the requirement for a user, other than the
attacker, to participate in the successful compromise the
vulnerable component. This metric determines whether the
vulnerability can be exploited solely at the will of the attacker,
or whether a separate user (or user-initiated process) must
participate in some manner.
None
The vulnerable system can be exploited without any interaction from any user.
Scope
Does a successful attack impact a component other than the
vulnerable component? If so, the Base Score increases and the
Confidentiality, Integrity and Authentication metrics should be
scored relative to the impacted component.
Unchanged
An exploited vulnerability can only affect resources managed by the same security authority. In this case, the vulnerable component and the
impacted component are either the same, or both are managed by the same security authority.
Confidentiality
This metric measures the impact to the confidentiality of the
information resources managed by a software component due
to a successfully exploited vulnerability. Confidentiality refers to
limiting information access and disclosure to only authorized
users, as well as preventing access by, or disclosure to,
unauthorized ones.
High
There is total loss of confidentiality, resulting in all resources within the impacted component being divulged to the attacker. Alternatively, access
to only some restricted information is obtained, but the disclosed information presents a direct, serious impact.
Integrity
This metric measures the impact to integrity of a successfully
exploited vulnerability. Integrity refers to the trustworthiness
and veracity of information.
High
There is a total loss of integrity, or a complete loss of protection. For example, the attacker is able to modify any/all files protected by the
impacted component. Alternatively, only some files can be modified, but malicious modification would present a direct, serious consequence to
the impacted component.
Availability
This metric measures the impact to the availability of the
impacted component resulting from a successfully exploited
vulnerability. It refers to the loss of availability of the impacted
component itself, such as a networked service (e.g., web,
database, email). Since availability refers to the accessibility of
information resources, attacks that consume network
bandwidth, processor cycles, or disk space all impact the
availability of an impacted component.
High
There is total loss of availability, resulting in the attacker being able to fully deny access to resources in the impacted component; this loss is
either sustained (while the attacker continues to deliver the attack) or persistent (the condition persists even after the attack has completed).
Alternatively, the attacker has the ability to deny some availability, but the loss of availability presents a direct, serious consequence to the
impacted component (e.g., the attacker cannot disrupt existing connections, but can prevent new connections; the attacker can repeatedly
exploit a vulnerability that, in each instance of a successful attack, leaks a only small amount of memory, but after repeated exploitation causes a
service to become completely unavailable).
Temporal score metrics (3)
Exploit Code Maturity
This metric measures the likelihood of the vulnerability being
attacked, and is typically based on the current state of exploit
techniques, public availability of exploit code, or active, 'in-the-
wild' exploitation.
Unproven
No publicly available exploit code is available, or an exploit is theoretical.
Remediation Level
The Remediation Level of a vulnerability is an important factor
for prioritization. The typical vulnerability is unpatched when
initially published. Workarounds or hotfixes may offer interim
remediation until an official patch or upgrade is issued. Each of
these respective stages adjusts the temporal score downwards,
reflecting the decreasing urgency as remediation becomes
final.
Official Fix
A complete vendor solution is available. Either the vendor has issued an official patch, or an upgrade is available.
Report Confidence
This metric measures the degree of confidence in the existence
of the vulnerability and the credibility of the known technical
details. Sometimes only the existence of vulnerabilities are
publicized, but without specific details. For example, an impact
may be recognized as undesirable, but the root cause may not
be known. The vulnerability may later be corroborated by
research which suggests where the vulnerability may lie,
though the research may not be certain. Finally, a vulnerability
may be confirmed through acknowledgement by the author or
vendor of the affected technology. The urgency of a
vulnerability is higher when a vulnerability is known to exist
with certainty. This metric also suggests the level of technical
knowledge available to would-be attackers.
Confirmed
Detailed reports exist, or functional reproduction is possible (functional exploits may provide this). Source code is available to independently
verify the assertions of the research, or the author or vendor of the affected code has confirmed the presence of the vulnerability.

content.text:
I could read everything. Two things needed a workaround:

- **Project_Design.docx** is locked, probably because it's open in Word. I read a copy.
- **The PDFs** can't be rendered here, so I extracted their text with a PDF library installed only in the scratch folder. `CISA KEV Search.pdf` is screenshots only, with no extractable text.

## Two things you need to act on

1. **Your Ollama key is rejected.** A chat call to Ollama Cloud returned `401 Unauthorized`. The key is formatted fine and `gemma4:31b` is on the model list, so the key is probably wrong or expired. Generate a new one at ollama.com and update `.env`. Nothing that calls the model can be tested until then.
2. **The Tavily key is now in this chat transcript.** I'll put it only in `.env`, which git ignores. Consider rotating it after the course.

The live sources all work today: the CVE API, NVD API 2.0 (status "Analyzed", Microsoft's 9.8 score) and the CISA KEV feed (this CVE is not listed).

## Mismatches between the design and the src files (fixed)

All 28 policy tests pass after these changes.

| File | Mismatch with the design | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `policy.py` | Your confidence rule (High / Medium / Low) wasn't implemented anywhere | Added `confidence()`: Low for P-IE, P-RV-C or P-RV-F; Medium if an assumption was used, a tool call failed, or reachability was defaulted; otherwise High |
| `policy.py` | Comment said the design doesn't set the order of the Gate 1 outcomes | Your workflow table does set it, and the code already follows it; the comment now cites the table |
| `policy.py` | Inputs missing C1–C3 were accepted silently | Missing conditions are now rejected |
| `validate.py` | Pointed to `assessment_schema.json`, which doesn't exist | Now uses `Resources/output_schema.json` |
| `validate.py` | One failed call to `environment_search` or `lookup_vulnerability` forced P-RV-F, even after a successful retry | P-RV-F now applies only when no call to that tool succeeded (all failed or never run), as in your tool-failure rules |
| `validate.py` | Evidence only had to name an existing tool call | Evidence must come from a successful call that also lists it ("every evidence item cites a validated source") |
| `validate.py` | Confidence wasn't checked | Now compared against `policy.py` |
| both test files | Wrong import paths, and `test_validate.py` loads a fixture that never existed | Paths fixed; new tests for confidence and the evidence link |

`test_validate.py` still can't run. `jsonschema` isn't installed, and it needs a schema-valid example assessment. Both are in Step 1 below.

**Decisions I need from you:**
- **A. Confidence for the baseline.** Under your design, P-IE gives **Low** confidence. Your expected JSON says **Medium**. I followed the design. Do you want that, or should the design rule change?
- **B. The expected JSON doesn't pass the schema.** Evidence IDs are filenames, `missing_decisive_facts` uses "C3: …" instead of `U1`, `tool_trace` is plain text, and `analyst_review.status` is `true`. I'll leave it as your human version and build a separate valid copy as a test example. Smaller issues in it:
  - The 9.8 score is attributed to NVD, but it's Microsoft's score as shown by NVD.
  - The NVD last-modified date should be 2026-09-24.
  - The environment path should be `Resources/`.
- **C. `.gitignore` ignores `*.docx`.** That means the design doc and environment doc won't go into the repo you submit. Should I add exceptions for those two files?

## Implementation plan

I recommend a plain Python loop over Ollama's tool-calling chat endpoint rather than a framework like LangGraph. It's the simplest setup that meets the brief, and each workflow step stays a visible function.

**Layout:** each item the assignment says to keep separate gets its own place.
```
src/config.py        model settings, paths, limits, allowed domains (reads .env)
src/sources/         raw access to CVE, NVD, KEV and Tavily: timeout, one retry, cache fallback
src/tools/           the 4 tool contracts, argument checks, tool list for the model, dispatch
src/llm.py           Ollama client
src/prompts.py       prompts for planning, fact extraction and explanation
src/orchestrator.py  the workflow table, step by step
src/assemble.py      builds the assessment JSON
src/policy.py, src/validate.py   rating logic and validation (existing)
run_assessment.py    command-line entry point
cache/               saved NVD record and KEV feed (the CVE JSON is already in Resources)
runs/<timestamp>/    inputs, config, raw tool outputs, tool log, model transcript, assessment
tests/               all tests and the example assessment
```

**Step 1 – Setup.**
- Pinned `requirements.txt`, virtual-environment steps, `config.py`, `.env.example`, and the Tavily key added to `.env`.
- Move the tests to `tests/` and build the schema-valid example assessment.
- Save today's NVD record and KEV feed into `cache/` as machine-readable fallbacks, since the PDFs can't serve that role.
- *Check:* the whole test suite passes, including `test_validate.py`.

**Step 2 – Source access.**
- Clients for CVE, NVD, KEV and Tavily, each with a timeout, one retry after a short pause, and the cached copy as fallback.
- Every result labelled `live` or `cached`, with the retrieval time and the reason a fallback was used.
- A config switch to force a source to fail, for the controlled-failure test.
- *Check:* unit tests with mocked responses, plus one live smoke test of each source.

**Step 3 – Tools.** Each tool follows your contract exactly:
- **`lookup_vulnerability`** merges CVE and NVD and flags conflicts in the CVSS vector or fixed builds.
- **`lookup_kev`** checks the KEV catalog.
- **`tavily_search`** enforces your allowed domains and a result cap.
- **`environment_search`** supports the `asset`, `text`, `flows` and `business_service` query types. Each returned record includes its location in the environment file, whether the fact is stated or inferred, its scenario evidence IDs, and which fields are unknown.
- Invalid arguments go back to the model once for correction; a second bad request fails. Every call is logged as T1, T2, … with its raw output saved.
- An invalid tool *name* can't appear in `tool_trace` because the schema only allows the four tools. I'll record those in the run log instead.
- *Check:* tests for each tool against the real environment file, including bad arguments.

**Step 4 – Model client.**
- Calls to `gemma4:31b` at temperature 0, with tool calling and JSON output for fact extraction, plus a timeout and retry.
- *Check:* one live call. This step is blocked until the Ollama key works.

**Step 5 – Orchestrator.** Implements your workflow table:
1. Intake.
2. Model plans tool calls, with follow-up rounds capped at 5.
3. Evidence completeness check, with one loop back.
4. Model extracts facts.
5. Code validates the facts, with one retry before P-RV-F.
6. Gate 1 and Gate 2 are scored in `policy.py`.
7. Model writes the explanation and cannot change any score.
8. Code assembles and validates the assessment and saves the run.

The model cites only tool call IDs and locators. Code then assigns E1, E2, … and fills in the source, URL, date and live/cached label from the tool log, so the model can't invent citations.
- *Check:* an end-to-end test with scripted model responses (repeatable, no network), then one real run.

**Step 6 – Full run and baseline.**
- A live run saved as the Assignment 2 baseline.
- A small `review.py` so a group member can approve or override the result, with a justification, as the analyst review.

"""Run configuration: non-secret settings from config/settings.json, secrets from .env.

Paths in settings.json are relative to the repository root so the project runs
from any working directory after a fresh clone.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import copy
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path

from dotenv import load_dotenv

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
SETTINGS_PATH = ROOT / "config" / "settings.json"
SECRET_KEYS = ("OLLAMA_API_KEY", "TAVILY_API_KEY")


def path(rel: str) -> Path:
    """Resolve a repo-relative path from settings.json."""
    return ROOT / rel


def load_settings(settings_path: Path = SETTINGS_PATH, overrides: dict | None = None) -> dict:
    """Load settings.json, apply .env model overrides, then caller overrides (e.g. --fail flags)."""
    load_dotenv(ROOT / ".env")
    s = json.loads(settings_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    if os.getenv("OLLAMA_MODEL"):
        s["model"]["name"] = os.environ["OLLAMA_MODEL"]
    for section, values in (overrides or {}).items():
        s[section].update(values)
    return s


def secret(name: str) -> str | None:
    """Read an API key. Returns None when unset so callers can fail with a clear message."""
    load_dotenv(ROOT / ".env")
    return os.getenv(name) or None


def redacted(settings: dict) -> dict:
    """Settings safe to save in a run folder (settings never hold secrets, but guard anyway)."""
    s = copy.deepcopy(settings)
    blob = json.dumps(s)
    for key in SECRET_KEYS:
        val = os.getenv(key)
        if val and val in blob:
            raise ValueError(f"{key} value found in settings; secrets belong in .env only")
    return s

"""Setup checks: a fresh clone has every input file the run needs, and caches match their manifest."""

import hashlib
import json

import config


def test_settings_load_and_hold_no_secrets():
    s = config.load_settings()
    config.redacted(s)  # raises if a key value leaked into settings
    assert s["model"]["temperature"] == 0
    assert not any(v for k, v in s["fault_injection"].items() if not k.startswith("$"))


def test_all_input_and_cache_paths_exist():
    s = config.load_settings()
    paths = [s["inputs"]["threat_input"]["path"], s["inputs"]["environment_snapshot"]["path"],
             s["paths"]["schema"], s["paths"]["cache_manifest"]]
    paths += [src["cache"] for src in s["sources"].values() if "cache" in src]
    missing = [p for p in paths if not config.path(p).is_file()]
    assert not missing, f"missing files: {missing}"


def test_cache_files_match_manifest_hashes():
    s = config.load_settings()
    manifest = json.loads(config.path(s["paths"]["cache_manifest"]).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    for rel, meta in manifest["files"].items():
        digest = hashlib.sha256(config.path(rel).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
        assert digest == meta["sha256"], f"{rel} changed since it was cached"

Step 1 is done and verified. The new Ollama key works: `gemma4:31b` returned a real tool call in the API's structured `tool_calls` field, not text in the reply. The Tavily key also works.

## What changed

- **Keys:** `.env` now holds the new Ollama key and the Tavily key. Git ignores it. `.env.example` is the template for anyone who clones the repo.
- **`.gitignore`:** I removed the `*.docx` rule, so both .docx files will be committed. `.env` and `.venv/` are still ignored, and `runs/` (the saved baseline) is not.
- **Dependencies:** a project virtual environment in `.venv`, with `requirements.txt` pinning requests 2.34.2, jsonschema 4.26.0, python-dotenv 1.2.4 and pytest 9.1.1 on Python 3.11.
- **Configuration:** `config/settings.json` holds the model settings, input paths, source URLs, your Tavily allowed domains, retry limits and the controlled-failure switches. It has no secrets and gets copied into every run folder. `src/config.py` loads it, with all paths relative to the repo so it runs from any clone.
- **Cached fallbacks:** I saved today's NVD record as `Resources/nvd_CVE-2026-69730.json`. `Resources/cache_manifest.json` records where each cached file (CVE, NVD, your KEV backup) came from, when it was saved, and a SHA-256 fingerprint.
- **Tests:** they now live in `tests/` and `pytest.ini` handles the import path. `test_config.py` is new; it checks that every input file exists, the settings contain no secrets, and the cached files haven't changed since they were saved.
- **Machine version of your expected JSON:** `tests/fixtures/assessment_example_CVE-2026-69730_W01.json`. It has the same decision as yours (P-IE, provisional P-H-L4I2), with confidence **Low** per the design.

**Verification:** all 43 tests pass, and `python src/validate.py` passes the example on all 10 checks. `git check-ignore` confirms nothing the run needs is ignored. I haven't done a real clone-and-run test yet; that's planned for Step 8.

## Making sure tool calls are real (built into Steps 3–6)

A model can write text that looks like a tool result without any tool running. These layers stop that:

1. **Only structured calls run.** The orchestrator accepts tool requests only from the API's `tool_calls` field. Plain text that mentions a tool, or contains JSON shaped like a tool result, is rejected and logged.
2. **Each result carries a receipt.** When code runs a tool, it records the call ID (T1, T2, …), the start and end times, and a SHA-256 fingerprint of the raw output, which is saved to `runs/<id>/tool_outputs/`.
   - For outside sources it also records the HTTP status, final URL and response size, plus Tavily's `request_id`.
   - The model only ever sees the code-assigned call ID. It can't create one.
3. **The model can't write provenance.** At fact extraction the model may only cite call IDs and locators. Code assigns E1, E2, … and fills in source, URL, date and live/cached label from the tool log.
4. **Code re-checks the facts the rating depends on.** Each one (CVSS vector, KEV status, OS, services, OS build, RTO, fixed build) is compared against the saved raw output of the call it cites. A mismatch fails fact validation; the model gets one retry, then the result is P-RV-F.
5. **New validator checks:**
   - Every trace entry has a raw output file whose fingerprint still matches.
   - Every call the model requested has exactly one trace entry, and the reverse.
   - At least one call is marked `selected_by: model`.
   - Both `environment_search` and `lookup_vulnerability` completed.
6. **Tests that try to cheat:** a scripted model replies with a fake tool result as text, cites a call ID that doesn't exist, and states a CVSS vector that differs from the tool output. All three must be caught.

## Step 2 – Source access (awaiting your approval)

- **Files:** `src/sources/` with clients for CVE, NVD, KEV and Tavily.
- **Behavior:** each client times out, retries once after a short pause, then falls back to the cached copy. Tavily has no cache, as in your design.
- **Labels:** every result is marked `live` or `cached`, with the retrieval time (the cache's saved time from the manifest when used), the reason for any fallback, and the HTTP details for the receipts above.
- **Controlled failure:** the switches in `config/settings.json` force a source to fail or disable caching, for the controlled-failure test.
- **Verification:** unit tests with mocked responses cover success, retry then success, retry then cache, and failure with no cache. Live smoke tests (marked `live`, so they can be skipped) hit each real API once.

from sources.base import SourceResult, fetch


def _cve_ids(data) -> list[str]:
    return [v["cve"]["id"] for v in data.get("vulnerabilities", [])]


def fetch_nvd(cve_id: str, settings: dict) -> SourceResult:
    url = settings["sources"]["nvd"]["url"].format(cve_id=cve_id)
    res = fetch("nvd", url, settings, cache_accepts=lambda d: cve_id in _cve_ids(d))
    # NVD answers an unknown CVE with HTTP 200 and totalResults = 0.
    if res.ok and cve_id not in _cve_ids(res.data):
        res.status = "not_found"
    return res

"""Source layer tests with a mocked network: retry, cache fallback, fault injection, receipts."""

import hashlib
import json

import pytest
import requests

import config
from sources import base, fetch_cve, fetch_kev, fetch_nvd, search_tavily

CVE = "CVE-2026-69730"


class FakeResponse:
    def __init__(self, status=200, body=None, url="https://example.test"):
        self.status_code = status
        self.url = url
        self.content = json.dumps(body if body is not None else {}).encode()
        self.text = self.content.decode()

    def json(self):
        return json.loads(self.content)


class FakeNetwork:
    """Returns queued responses (or raises queued exceptions) and records every call."""

    def __init__(self, *outcomes):
        self.outcomes = list(outcomes)
        self.calls = []

    def __call__(self, method, url, **kw):
        self.calls.append((method, url, kw))
        out = self.outcomes.pop(0)
        if isinstance(out, Exception):
            raise out
        return out


@pytest.fixture
def settings():
    s = config.load_settings()
    s["retry"]["backoff_s"] = 0
    return s


@pytest.fixture
def net(monkeypatch):
    def install(*outcomes):
        fake = FakeNetwork(*outcomes)
        monkeypatch.setattr(base, "_send", fake)
        return fake
    monkeypatch.setattr(base, "_sleep", lambda s: None)
    return install


def cve_body(cve_id=CVE):
    return {"cveMetadata": {"cveId": cve_id}, "containers": {}}


TIMEOUT = requests.Timeout("read timed out")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- retry and cache

def test_live_success_has_receipt(settings, net):
    fake = net(FakeResponse(200, cve_body(), url="https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/" + CVE))
    r = fetch_cve(CVE, settings)
    assert (r.status, r.mode, r.attempts) == ("ok", "live", 1)
    assert r.receipt["http_status"] == 200
    assert r.receipt["sha256"] == hashlib.sha256(r.raw).hexdigest()
    assert len(fake.calls) == 1


def test_retry_then_success(settings, net):
    fake = net(TIMEOUT, FakeResponse(200, cve_body()))
    r = fetch_cve(CVE, settings)
    assert (r.status, r.mode, r.attempts) == ("ok", "live", 2)
    assert len(fake.calls) == 2


def test_two_failures_fall_back_to_cache(settings, net):
    net(TIMEOUT, FakeResponse(503, {"error": "down"}))
    r = fetch_cve(CVE, settings)
    manifest = json.loads(config.path(settings["paths"]["cache_manifest"]).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    meta = manifest["files"][settings["sources"]["cve"]["cache"]]
    assert (r.status, r.mode, r.attempts) == ("ok", "cached", 2)
    assert r.retrieved_at == meta["saved_at"]           # cached data is dated by when it was saved
    assert r.receipt["sha256"] == meta["sha256"]
    assert "HTTP 503" in r.fallback_reason
    assert r.data["cveMetadata"]["cveId"] == CVE


def test_two_failures_without_cache_fail(settings, net):
    settings["fault_injection"]["disable_cache"] = True
    net(TIMEOUT, TIMEOUT)
    r = fetch_cve(CVE, settings)
    assert (r.status, r.mode, r.data) == ("failed", None, None)
    assert "no cached fallback" in r.error


def test_404_is_not_found_without_retry_or_cache(settings, net):
    fake = net(FakeResponse(404, {"error": "CVE_RECORD_DNE"}))
    r = fetch_cve("CVE-2099-0001", settings)
    assert (r.status, r.mode) == ("not_found", "live")
    assert len(fake.calls) == 1


def test_client_error_is_not_retried_but_uses_cache(settings, net):
    fake = net(FakeResponse(403, {"error": "forbidden"}))
    r = fetch_nvd(CVE, settings)
    assert len(fake.calls) == 1
    assert (r.status, r.mode) == ("ok", "cached")


def test_cache_for_a_different_cve_is_not_used(settings, net):
    net(TIMEOUT, TIMEOUT)
    r = fetch_cve("CVE-2026-00001", settings)
    assert r.status == "failed"
    assert "does not cover this request" in r.error


def test_tampered_cache_is_rejected(settings, net, monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    manifest = json.loads(config.path(settings["paths"]["cache_manifest"]).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    manifest["files"][settings["sources"]["cve"]["cache"]]["sha256"] = "0" * 64
    fake_manifest = tmp_path / "manifest.json"
    fake_manifest.write_text(json.dumps(manifest))
    settings["paths"]["cache_manifest"] = str(fake_manifest)  # absolute path; config.path keeps it
    net(TIMEOUT, TIMEOUT)
    r = fetch_cve(CVE, settings)
    assert r.status == "failed"
    assert "SHA-256 does not match" in r.error


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- fault injection

def test_fault_injection_never_touches_the_network(settings, net):

    r = fetch_kev(settings)
    assert fake.calls == []
    assert (r.status, r.mode, r.attempts) == ("ok", "cached", 2)

def test_tavily_has_no_cache(settings, net, monkeypatch):

    assert search_tavily("q", ["cisa.gov"], 3, settings).status == "not_found"

    monkeypatch.setattr(config, "secret", lambda name: None)
    fake = net()

    r = fetch_cve(CVE, config.load_settings())
    assert (r.status, r.mode) == ("ok", "live") and r.receipt["http_status"] == 200


@pytest.mark.live
def test_live_nvd():
    r = fetch_nvd(CVE, config.load_settings())
    assert (r.status, r.mode) == ("ok", "live")


@pytest.mark.live
def test_live_kev():
    r = fetch_kev(config.load_settings())
    assert (r.status, r.mode) == ("ok", "live") and r.data["count"] > 1000


@pytest.mark.live
def test_live_tavily():

    assert r.status == "ok" and r.receipt["request_id"]

Step 2 is done and verified: 58 offline tests and 4 live tests pass.

## What I built (`src/sources/`)

- **`base.py`** handles retry, cache and receipts for every source:
  - **Retry:** each source gets up to 2 attempts with a pause between them. Errors that won't change on a retry (400, 401, 403, 422) aren't retried. A 404 is treated as "not found", with no retry and no cache.
  - **Cache fallback:** used only if the cached file matches its fingerprint in `cache_manifest.json` and actually covers the request (a different CVE ID is refused). Cached results are dated by when the cache was saved, not by today's date, and carry the reason the fallback was used.
  - **Receipts:** a live result records the HTTP status, final URL, size, SHA-256 fingerprint and response time; a cached one records the cache path, fingerprint and saved date. Step 3 copies these into the tool trace as proof each call really happened.
  - **Controlled failure:** when a failure switch is on, the network is never contacted. A test confirms zero network calls.
- **`cve.py`, `nvd.py`, `kev.py`, `tavily.py`** are the clients for each source:
  - NVD reports an unknown CVE as an empty result, which is treated as "not found".
  - KEV returns the whole catalog; Step 3's `lookup_kev` searches it for the CVE.
  - Tavily is live only, records its `request_id`, and fails cleanly if the key is missing.

## What the live run showed

- CVE and NVD came back live on the first try.
- With the NVD failure switch on, the cached copy was used, dated by its saved time, with the reason recorded.
- The live CVE record and your cached copy have identical content; the size gap is only formatting. So comparing them in Step 3 won't flag false conflicts.

## Step 3 – Tools (awaiting your approval)

The four tools in `src/tools/` follow your contracts exactly.

**`lookup_vulnerability`**
- Merges CVE and NVD into one result: description, weakness (CWE), NVD status, CVSS score and its metrics, affected products and fixed builds.
- Flags a conflict when the two sources disagree on the CVSS base metrics or on the fixed build for Windows Server 2022.
- Marks the result `live`, `cached` or `mixed`. If one source fails it uses the other and says so; if both fail with no cache, it returns failed.

**`lookup_kev`**
- Returns the KEV fields from your contract (in KEV or not, date added, required action, due date, ransomware use), plus the catalog version.

**`tavily_search`**
- The model writes the query and picks domains.
- Code accepts only domains from your allowed list and caps the result count.

**`environment_search`**
- Supports the `asset`, `text`, `flows` and `business_service` query types.
- Each record says where it sits in the environment file (e.g. `assets[asset_id=W01]`), whether the fact is stated or inferred, its scenario evidence IDs and its unknown fields.
- Explicit absence statements and the S06 completeness record are included, so the agent can confirm W01 is the only DNS server.

**Tool registry** (`registry.py`)
- Holds the tool descriptions sent to the model and checks every request's arguments.
- One bad request goes back to the model as an error to correct; a second bad request for the same tool is marked failed.
- Each call gets a code-assigned ID (T1, T2, …), its raw output saved to `runs/<id>/tool_outputs/T#.json` with a fingerprint, and a trace entry.
- The model receives a compact result that includes the call ID, not raw data. For example, never the whole 1.7 MB KEV catalog.

**Tests**
- Each tool runs against the real environment file and the cached sources.
- Bad arguments, a disallowed domain, an unknown tool name, and the second-bad-request rule are all tested.
- A conflict test uses a changed copy of the NVD cache.
- A test confirms each saved output's fingerprint matches its trace entry.

"""lookup_kev: is the CVE in the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog?

Contract (design doc):
  in : {"cve_id": str}
  out: {status: found|not_found|failed, in_kev, date_added, known_ransomware_use, required_action,
        due_date, source_url, retrieved_at, mode: live|cached}
Role: in_kev = true sets exploit activity to 2. Absence from KEV does not establish safety.
On failure: retry once, then the cached feed; with no cache, status=failed and in_kev=null.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from sources import fetch_kev
from tools.base import ToolOutput, receipt_of


def run(args: dict, settings: dict) -> ToolOutput:
    cve_id = args["cve_id"]
    res = fetch_kev(settings)
    receipts = [receipt_of(res)]
    base = {"cve_id": cve_id, "source_url": settings["sources"]["kev"]["url"], "retrieved_at": res.retrieved_at, "mode": res.mode}

    if not res.ok:
        result = {"status": "failed", "in_kev": None, "date_added": None, "known_ransomware_use": None,
                  "required_action": None, "due_date": None, **base}
        return ToolOutput(result, "failed", None, max(res.attempts, 1), res.status == "failed", f"KEV lookup failed: {res.error}",
                          res.error, receipts)

    feed = res.data
    entry = next((v for v in feed["vulnerabilities"] if v.get("cveID") == cve_id), None)
    catalog = {"catalog_version": feed.get("catalogVersion"), "date_released": feed.get("dateReleased"), "count": feed.get("count")}
    result = {
        "status": "found" if entry else "not_found",
        "in_kev": entry is not None,
        "date_added": entry and entry.get("dateAdded"),
        "known_ransomware_use": entry and entry.get("knownRansomwareCampaignUse"),
        "required_action": entry and entry.get("requiredAction"),
        "due_date": entry and entry.get("dueDate"),
        **base,
        "catalog": catalog,
        "fallback_reason": res.fallback_reason,
        "locator": f"vulnerabilities[cveID={cve_id}]" + ("" if entry else " (no match)"),
        "note": None if entry else "Absence from KEV does not establish that the CVE is not exploited.",
    }
    summary = f"{cve_id} {'IS' if entry else 'is not'} in KEV (catalog {catalog['catalog_version']}, {res.mode})"
    # Save the catalog metadata and the matching entry, not the whole 1.7 MB feed; the receipt holds the feed hash.
    return ToolOutput(result, result["status"], res.mode, max(res.attempts, 1), res.mode == "cached", summary, None, receipts,
                      source_raw={"kev_catalog": catalog, "kev_entry": entry})

"""Source layer tests with a mocked network: retry, cache fallback, fault injection, receipts."""

import hashlib
import json

import pytest
import requests

import config
from sources import base, fetch_cve, fetch_kev, fetch_nvd, search_tavily

CVE = "CVE-2026-69730"


class FakeResponse:
    def __init__(self, status=200, body=None, url="https://example.test"):
        self.status_code = status
        self.url = url
        self.content = json.dumps(body if body is not None else {}).encode()
        self.text = self.content.decode()

    def json(self):
        return json.loads(self.content)


class FakeNetwork:
    """Returns queued responses (or raises queued exceptions) and records every call."""

    def __init__(self, *outcomes):
        self.outcomes = list(outcomes)
        self.calls = []

    def __call__(self, method, url, **kw):
        self.calls.append((method, url, kw))
        out = self.outcomes.pop(0)
        if isinstance(out, Exception):
            raise out
        return out


@pytest.fixture
def settings():
    s = config.load_settings()
    s["retry"]["backoff_s"] = 0
    return s


@pytest.fixture
def net(monkeypatch):
    def install(*outcomes):
        fake = FakeNetwork(*outcomes)
        monkeypatch.setattr(base, "_send", fake)
        return fake
    monkeypatch.setattr(base, "_sleep", lambda s: None)
    return install


def cve_body(cve_id=CVE):
    return {"cveMetadata": {"cveId": cve_id}, "containers": {}}


TIMEOUT = requests.Timeout("read timed out")


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- retry and cache

def test_live_success_has_receipt(settings, net):
    fake = net(FakeResponse(200, cve_body(), url="https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/" + CVE))
    r = fetch_cve(CVE, settings)
    assert (r.status, r.mode, r.attempts) == ("ok", "live", 1)
    assert r.receipt["http_status"] == 200
    assert r.receipt["sha256"] == hashlib.sha256(r.raw).hexdigest()
    assert len(fake.calls) == 1


def test_retry_then_success(settings, net):
    fake = net(TIMEOUT, FakeResponse(200, cve_body()))
    r = fetch_cve(CVE, settings)
    assert (r.status, r.mode, r.attempts) == ("ok", "live", 2)
    assert len(fake.calls) == 2


def test_two_failures_fall_back_to_cache(settings, net):
    net(TIMEOUT, FakeResponse(503, {"error": "down"}))
    r = fetch_cve(CVE, settings)
    manifest = json.loads(config.path(settings["paths"]["cache_manifest"]).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    meta = manifest["files"][settings["sources"]["cve"]["cache"]]
    assert (r.status, r.mode, r.attempts) == ("ok", "cached", 2)
    assert r.retrieved_at == meta["saved_at"]           # cached data is dated by when it was saved
    assert r.receipt["sha256"] == meta["sha256"]
    assert "HTTP 503" in r.fallback_reason
    assert r.data["cveMetadata"]["cveId"] == CVE


def test_two_failures_without_cache_fail(settings, net):
    settings["fault_injection"]["disable_cache"] = True
    net(TIMEOUT, TIMEOUT)
    r = fetch_cve(CVE, settings)
    assert (r.status, r.mode, r.data) == ("failed", None, None)
    assert "no cached fallback" in r.error


def test_404_is_not_found_without_retry_or_cache(settings, net):
    fake = net(FakeResponse(404, {"error": "CVE_RECORD_DNE"}))
    r = fetch_cve("CVE-2099-0001", settings)
    assert (r.status, r.mode) == ("not_found", "live")
    assert len(fake.calls) == 1


def test_client_error_is_not_retried_but_uses_cache(settings, net):
    fake = net(FakeResponse(403, {"error": "forbidden"}))
    r = fetch_nvd(CVE, settings)
    assert len(fake.calls) == 1
    assert (r.status, r.mode) == ("ok", "cached")


def test_cache_for_a_different_cve_is_not_used(settings, net):
    net(TIMEOUT, TIMEOUT)
    r = fetch_cve("CVE-2026-00001", settings)
    assert r.status == "failed"
    assert "does not cover this request" in r.error


def test_tampered_cache_is_rejected(settings, net, monkeypatch, tmp_path):
    manifest = json.loads(config.path(settings["paths"]["cache_manifest"]).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    manifest["files"][settings["sources"]["cve"]["cache"]]["sha256"] = "0" * 64
    fake_manifest = tmp_path / "manifest.json"
    fake_manifest.write_text(json.dumps(manifest))
    settings["paths"]["cache_manifest"] = str(fake_manifest)  # absolute path; config.path keeps it
    net(TIMEOUT, TIMEOUT)
    r = fetch_cve(CVE, settings)
    assert r.status == "failed"
    assert "SHA-256 does not match" in r.error


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- fault injection

def test_fault_injection_never_touches_the_network(settings, net):
    settings["fault_injection"]["kev"] = True
    fake = net()  # any network call would pop from an empty list and error
    r = fetch_kev(settings)
    assert fake.calls == []
    assert (r.status, r.mode, r.attempts) == ("ok", "cached", 2)
    assert "fault injection" in r.fallback_reason


def test_fault_injection_with_cache_disabled_fails(settings, net):
    settings["fault_injection"].update(cve=True, disable_cache=True)
    net()
    r = fetch_cve(CVE, settings)
    assert r.status == "failed" and "fault injection" in r.error


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- source-specific

def test_nvd_empty_result_is_not_found(settings, net):
    net(FakeResponse(200, {"totalResults": 0, "vulnerabilities": []}))
    assert fetch_nvd(CVE, settings).status == "not_found"


def test_tavily_has_no_cache(settings, net, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("TAVILY_API_KEY", "test-key")
    net(TIMEOUT, TIMEOUT)
    r = search_tavily("q", ["cisa.gov"], 3, settings)
    assert (r.status, r.mode, r.attempts) == ("failed", None, 2)


def test_tavily_records_request_id_and_sends_domains(settings, net, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("TAVILY_API_KEY", "test-key")
    fake = net(FakeResponse(200, {"results": [{"url": "https://cisa.gov/x"}], "request_id": "req-123"}))
    r = search_tavily("q", ["cisa.gov"], 3, settings)
    assert r.receipt["request_id"] == "req-123"
    body = fake.calls[0][2]["json"]
    assert body["include_domains"] == ["cisa.gov"] and body["max_results"] == 3
    assert fake.calls[0][2]["headers"]["Authorization"] == "Bearer test-key"


def test_tavily_empty_results_is_not_found(settings, net, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("TAVILY_API_KEY", "test-key")
    net(FakeResponse(200, {"results": [], "request_id": "r"}))
    assert search_tavily("q", ["cisa.gov"], 3, settings).status == "not_found"


def test_tavily_missing_key_fails_cleanly(settings, net, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(config, "secret", lambda name: None)
    fake = net()
    r = search_tavily("q", ["cisa.gov"], 3, settings)
    assert r.status == "failed" and "TAVILY_API_KEY" in r.error and fake.calls == []

@pytest.mark.live
def test_live_cve():
    r = fetch_cve(CVE, config.load_settings())
    assert (r.status, r.mode) == ("ok", "live") and r.receipt["http_status"] == 200


@pytest.mark.live
def test_live_nvd():
    r = fetch_nvd(CVE, config.load_settings())
    assert (r.status, r.mode) == ("ok", "live")
