"""Tool contract tests (offline). External sources are served from the caches via fault injection
or from a fake network; environment_search runs on the real environment snapshot."""

import hashlib
import json

import pytest

import config
from fakes import FakeResponse
from tools import environment_search, lookup_kev, lookup_vulnerability, tavily_search
from tools.registry import ToolRunner, load_raw_output
from validate import check_raw_outputs, check_tool_contracts

CVE = "CVE-2026-69730"
ENV_PATH = "Resources/windows_enterprise_environment.json"


@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
def env():
    return json.loads(config.path(ENV_PATH).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


@pytest.fixture
def cached(settings, net):
    """Settings where CVE, NVD and KEV are 'down', so tools use the caches with no network."""
    settings["fault_injection"].update(cve=True, nvd=True, kev=True)
    net()  # any real network call would raise
    return settings


def search(env, qtype, query, max_results=10):
    return environment_search.run({"query_type": qtype, "query": query, "max_results": max_results}, env, ENV_PATH)


def cache_json(settings, source):
    return json.loads(config.path(settings["sources"][source]["cache"]).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- environment_search

def test_env_asset_w01(env):
    out = search(env, "asset", "W01")
    rec = out.result["records"][0]
    assert (out.status, out.mode, len(out.result["records"])) == ("found", "simulated", 1)
    assert rec["locator"] == "assets[asset_id=W01]" and rec["basis"] == "stated"
    assert {"platform.os_build", "platform.installed_kbs"} <= set(rec["unknown_fields"])
    assert rec["data"]["platform"]["os"] == "Windows Server 2022"
    assert "DNS Server" in rec["data"]["services"]


def test_env_text_dns_server_only_w01_with_completeness(env):
    out = search(env, "text", "DNS Server")
    cov = out.result["coverage"]
    assert cov["matching_asset_ids"] == ["W01"] and cov["assets_searched"] == 44
    assert "complete at cohort level" in cov["completeness_statement"]
    assert cov["completeness_locator"] == "evidence[evidence_id=S06]"


def test_env_flows_w01(env):
    recs = search(env, "flows", "W01", max_results=25).result["records"]
    ids = {r["record_id"] for r in recs}
    assert {"F09", "F10", "IDENTITY", "network.default_policy", "network.public_services"} <= ids
    assert any(r["record_type"] == "denied_path" and "W08" in r["data"]["source"] for r in recs)
    public = next(r for r in recs if r["record_type"] == "public_exposure")
    assert "DNS" in public["data"]["not_published_to_internet"]


def test_env_business_service_by_asset(env):
    recs = search(env, "business_service", "W01").result["records"]
    bs01 = next(r for r in recs if r["record_id"] == "BS01")
    assert bs01["data"]["rto_hours"] == 4 and bs01["locator"] == "business_services[service_id=BS01]"


def test_env_not_found_and_truncation(env):
    assert search(env, "asset", "Z99").status == "not_found"
    out = search(env, "text", "W01", max_results=2)
    assert len(out.result["records"]) == 2 and out.result["truncated"] > 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- lookup_vulnerability

def test_vuln_from_caches(cached):
    out = lookup_vulnerability.run({"cve_id": CVE}, cached)
    r = out.result
    assert (out.status, out.mode, out.fallback_used, out.attempts) == ("found", "cached", True, 2)
    assert r["cvss"]["base_score"] == 9.8
    assert r["cvss"]["metrics"] == {"AV": "N", "AC": "L", "PR": "N", "UI": "N", "S": "U", "C": "H", "I": "H", "A": "H"}
    assert r["cvss"]["temporal"]["exploit_code_maturity"] == "U"
    s2022 = next(a for a in r["affected"] if a["product"] == "Windows Server 2022")

@pytest.fixture
def cached(settings, net):

    settings["fault_injection"].update(cve=True, nvd=True, kev=True)
    net()  # any real network call would raise
    return settings


def search(env, qtype, query, max_results=10):
    return environment_search.run({"query_type": qtype, "query": query, "max_results": max_results}, env, ENV_PATH)


def cache_json(settings, source):
    return json.loads(config.path(settings["sources"][source]["cache"]).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- environment_search

def test_env_asset_w01(env):
    out = search(env, "asset", "W01")
    rec = out.result["records"][0]
    assert (out.status, out.mode, len(out.result["records"])) == ("found", "simulated", 1)
    assert rec["locator"] == "assets[asset_id=W01]" and rec["basis"] == "stated"
    assert {"platform.os_build", "platform.installed_kbs"} <= set(rec["unknown_fields"])
    assert rec["data"]["platform"]["os"] == "Windows Server 2022"
    assert "DNS Server" in rec["data"]["services"]


def test_env_text_dns_server_only_w01_with_completeness(env):
    out = search(env, "text", "DNS Server")
    cov = out.result["coverage"]
    assert cov["matching_asset_ids"] == ["W01"] and cov["assets_searched"] == 44
    assert "complete at cohort level" in cov["completeness_statement"]
    assert cov["completeness_locator"] == "evidence[evidence_id=S06]"


def test_env_flows_w01(env):
    recs = search(env, "flows", "W01", max_results=25).result["records"]
    ids = {r["record_id"] for r in recs}
    assert {"F09", "F10", "IDENTITY", "network.default_policy", "network.public_services"} <= ids
    assert any(r["record_type"] == "denied_path" and "W08" in r["data"]["source"] for r in recs)
    public = next(r for r in recs if r["record_type"] == "public_exposure")
    assert "DNS" in public["data"]["not_published_to_internet"]


def test_env_business_service_by_asset(env):
    recs = search(env, "business_service", "W01").result["records"]
    bs01 = next(r for r in recs if r["record_id"] == "BS01")
    assert bs01["data"]["rto_hours"] == 4 and bs01["locator"] == "business_services[service_id=BS01]"


def test_env_not_found_and_truncation(env):
    assert search(env, "asset", "Z99").status == "not_found"
    out = search(env, "text", "W01", max_results=2)
    assert len(out.result["records"]) == 2 and out.result["truncated"] > 0


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- lookup_vulnerability

def test_vuln_from_caches(cached):
    out = lookup_vulnerability.run({"cve_id": CVE}, cached)
    r = out.result
    assert (out.status, out.mode, out.fallback_used, out.attempts) == ("found", "cached", True, 2)
    assert r["cvss"]["base_score"] == 9.8
    assert r["cvss"]["metrics"] == {"AV": "N", "AC": "L", "PR": "N", "UI": "N", "S": "U", "C": "H", "I": "H", "A": "H"}
    assert r["cvss"]["temporal"]["exploit_code_maturity"] == "U"
    s2022 = next(a for a in r["affected"] if a["product"] == "Windows Server 2022")
    assert s2022 == {"product": "Windows Server 2022", "version_start": "10.0.20348.0", "fixed_build": "10.0.20348.5622"}
    assert r["conflicts"] == []
    assert r["ssvc"]["Exploitation"] == "none"
    assert r["cwe"] == ["CWE-416"]
    assert all(s["mode"] == "cached" and s["fallback_reason"] for s in r["sources"])
    assert out.source_raw["cve"] and out.source_raw["nvd"]


def test_vuln_mixed_live_and_cached(settings, net):
    settings["fault_injection"]["nvd"] = True
    net(routes={"cveawg": FakeResponse(200, cache_json(settings, "cve"))})
    out = lookup_vulnerability.run({"cve_id": CVE}, settings)
    assert (out.status, out.mode) == ("found", "mixed")


def test_vuln_one_source_failed_uses_the_other(settings, net):
    settings["fault_injection"].update(cve=True, disable_cache=True)
    net(routes={"services.nvd": FakeResponse(200, cache_json(settings, "nvd"))})
    out = lookup_vulnerability.run({"cve_id": CVE}, settings)
    assert (out.status, out.mode, out.fallback_used) == ("found", "live", True)
    assert any(n.startswith("CVE failed") for n in out.result["notes"])
    assert out.result["cvss"]["vector"].startswith("CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N")


def test_vuln_both_failed_no_cache(settings, net):

    net()
    out = lookup_vulnerability.run({"cve_id": CVE}, settings)
    assert (out.status, out.mode, out.result["status"]) == ("failed", None, "failed")
    assert "CVE:" in out.error and "NVD:" in out.error


def test_vuln_conflicting_fixed_build_is_flagged(cached, tmp_path):
    nvd = cache_json(cached, "nvd")
    for node in nvd["vulnerabilities"][0]["cve"]["configurations"][0]["nodes"]:
        for cm in node["cpeMatch"]:
            if "windows_server_2022" in cm["criteria"]:
                cm["versionEndExcluding"] = "10.0.20348.5700"
    bad = tmp_path / "nvd_conflict.json"
    bad.write_text(json.dumps(nvd))
    manifest = json.loads(config.path(cached["paths"]["cache_manifest"]).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    manifest["files"][str(bad)] = {"source": "nvd", "saved_at": "2026-10-11T00:00:00-04:00",
                                   "sha256": hashlib.sha256(bad.read_bytes()).hexdigest()}
    (tmp_path / "manifest.json").write_text(json.dumps(manifest))
    cached["sources"]["nvd"]["cache"] = str(bad)
    cached["paths"]["cache_manifest"] = str(tmp_path / "manifest.json")
    out = lookup_vulnerability.run({"cve_id": CVE}, cached)
    assert len(out.result["conflicts"]) == 1
    assert "Windows Server 2022" in out.result["conflicts"][0] and "10.0.20348.5700" in out.result["conflicts"][0]

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- tavily_search

def test_tavily_drops_results_off_allowlist(settings, net, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("TAVILY_API_KEY", "k")
    net(routes={"tavily": FakeResponse(200, {"request_id": "r1", "results": [
        {"title": "MSRC", "url": "https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/" + CVE, "content": "x" * 2000},
        {"title": "blog", "url": "https://random-blog.example/post", "content": "exploit!"}]})})
    out = tavily_search.run({"query": CVE, "allowed_domains": ["msrc.microsoft.com"], "max_results": 5}, settings)
    assert (out.status, out.mode) == ("found", "live")
    assert [r["title"] for r in out.result["results"]] == ["MSRC"]
    assert out.result["dropped_off_allowlist"] == 1 and len(out.result["results"][0]["snippet"]) == 700
    assert out.result["request_id"] == "r1"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- registry / runner

@pytest.fixture
def runner(cached, env, tmp_path):
    return ToolRunner(cached, env, ENV_PATH, tmp_path / "tool_outputs")


def test_runner_assigns_ids_and_saves_verifiable_raw_output(runner):
    p1 = runner.execute("environment_search", {"query_type": "asset", "query": "W01"}, model_call_id="call_a")
    p2 = runner.execute("lookup_kev", '{"cve_id": "CVE-2026-69730"}', model_call_id="call_b")  # string args are parsed
    assert (p1["call_id"], p2["call_id"]) == ("T1", "T2")
    t1, t2 = runner.trace
    assert t1["model_call_id"] == "call_a" and t2["arguments"] == {"cve_id": CVE}
    raw = load_raw_output(t1)
    assert raw["call_id"] == "T1" and raw["result"]["records"][0]["record_id"] == "W01"
    assert t2["receipts"][0]["mode"] == "cached" and t2["receipts"][0]["sha256"]
    assert check_raw_outputs({"tool_trace": runner.trace}) == []


def test_runner_detects_tampered_raw_output(runner):
    runner.execute("lookup_kev", {"cve_id": CVE})
    path = config.ROOT / runner.trace[0]["raw_output_path"] if not runner.trace[0]["raw_output_path"].startswith(("/", "C:", "c:")) \
        else runner.trace[0]["raw_output_path"]
    raw = json.loads(open(path, encoding="utf-8").read())
    raw["result"]["in_kev"] = True
    open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(json.dumps(raw))
    assert any("SHA-256" in p for p in check_raw_outputs({"tool_trace": runner.trace}))


def test_runner_invalid_args_one_correction_then_failed(runner):
    p1 = runner.execute("environment_search", {"query_type": "assets", "query": "W01"})
    p2 = runner.execute("environment_search", {"query_type": "asset"})
    p3 = runner.execute("environment_search", {"query_type": "asset", "query": "W01"})
    assert (p1["status"], p2["status"], p3["status"]) == ("invalid_request", "failed", "found")
    assert "query_type" in p1["error"] and "one correction" in p1["error"]
    assert check_tool_contracts({"tool_trace": runner.trace}) == []

def test_runner_rejects_bad_cve_id_and_extra_args(runner):

    assert runner.trace == [] and runner.rejected[0]["tool"] == "search_exploits"
    assert runner.execute("search_exploits", {})["status"] == "failed"

## What I built (`src/tools/`)

- **`environment_search`** searches your environment JSON by asset, free text, network flows or business service. The key results on your data:
  - `asset "W01"` returns the W01 record with its location in the file. It shows the facts are stated, not inferred, and lists the OS build and installed KBs as unknown.
  - `text "DNS Server"` reports that W01 is the only matching asset out of 44, with the S06 statement that the asset register is complete at cohort level. That backs up your scope check.
  - `flows "W01"` returns flows F09 and F10, the denied path from the W08 jump hosts, the IDENTITY zone, the deny-by-default policy, and the published services, which confirm DNS isn't exposed to the Internet.
  - `business_service "W01"` returns BS01 with its 4-hour RTO.
- **`lookup_vulnerability`** merges CVE and NVD into one result:
  - Live today: CVSS 9.8 `AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/…/C:H/I:H/A:H`, Windows Server 2022 fixed at 10.0.20348.5622, no conflicts.
  - It also returns Microsoft's "Exploit Code Maturity: Unproven" rating and CISA's "Exploitation: none" assessment, both useful evidence for exploit activity.
  - A test with a changed copy of the NVD cache confirms a fixed-build disagreement is flagged as a conflict.
- **`lookup_kev`** reports "not in KEV" with catalog version 2026.10.08. It saves only the matching entry, plus a fingerprint of the full feed.
- **`tavily_search`** rejects domains that aren't on your allowed list and drops any result from a domain outside it. In live searches it found:
  - MSRC's "Exploitation More Likely" rating.
  - Microsoft's KB page confirming KB5122882 = build 20348.5622.
  - No exploitation reports from security vendors.
- **`registry.py`** is the only path from a model request to a tool:
  - It checks every argument against the tool's contract.
  - One bad request goes back to the model to correct; a second for the same tool is marked failed.
  - An unknown tool name never runs and is logged separately.
  - Each call gets a code-assigned ID (T1, T2, …). Its raw output is saved to a file with a fingerprint, and a trace entry records the model's own call ID, timestamps and source receipts.

## Changes to existing files

- `validate.py` has a new check: each raw output file must exist, match its saved fingerprint, and match its trace entry (call ID, tool, arguments, status). A test edits a saved output after the run and the check catches it.
- `validate.py` no longer checks arguments on failed calls, since those are rejected requests and produce no evidence.
- The shared test fixtures moved to `tests/conftest.py` and `tests/fakes.py`.

## Step 4 – Model client (awaiting your approval)

`src/llm.py` will make the calls to `gemma4:31b` on Ollama Cloud at temperature 0.

- **Two kinds of call:** a tool-calling chat for planning, and a JSON-schema-constrained call for fact extraction (Ollama supports a schema in its `format` field).
- **Failures:** a timeout plus one retry on network errors or server errors, then a clear failure.
- **Transcript:** every request and reply is saved to `model_transcript.jsonl` in the run folder, so the transcript shows exactly which tool calls the model asked for.
- **Fake-result detector:** if the model replies with text instead of a real tool call, and that text names a tool, cites a call ID, or contains JSON shaped like a tool result, the reply is flagged.
- **Scripted test model:** a stand-in model for the Step 5 tests, so the whole workflow can be tested without the network.
- **Verification:**
  - Mocked tests cover tool-call parsing (including arguments sent as a string), retry, and the detector.
  - Live tests check that the model makes a real `lookup_kev` tool call and that the JSON call returns output matching the schema.

"""Model client tests: request shape, tool-call parsing, retry, transcript, fabricated-output detection."""

import json

import pytest
import requests

import config
import llm
from fakes import FakeNetwork, FakeResponse
from llm import LLMError, OllamaClient, detect_fabricated_tool_output
from tools.registry import tool_specs, validate_arguments

TOOLS = ["environment_search", "lookup_vulnerability", "lookup_kev", "tavily_search"]


@pytest.fixture
def post(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("OLLAMA_API_KEY", "test-key")
    monkeypatch.setattr(llm, "_sleep", lambda s: None)

    def install(*outcomes):
        fake = FakeNetwork(*outcomes)
        monkeypatch.setattr(llm, "_post", lambda url, **kw: fake("POST", url, **kw))
        return fake
    return install


def ollama_body(content="", tool_calls=None):
    msg = {"role": "assistant", "content": content}
    if tool_calls is not None:
        msg["tool_calls"] = tool_calls
    return {"model": "gemma4:31b", "message": msg, "done": True}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- request and parsing

def test_request_shape_and_tool_call_parsing(settings, post, tmp_path):
    fake = post(FakeResponse(200, ollama_body(tool_calls=[
        {"id": "call_1", "function": {"name": "lookup_kev", "arguments": {"cve_id": "CVE-2026-69730"}}}])))
    client = OllamaClient(settings, tmp_path / "t.jsonl")
    r = client.chat([{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}], tools=tool_specs(settings), purpose="plan")
    body = fake.calls[0][2]["json"]
    assert body["options"]["temperature"] == 0 and body["stream"] is False and len(body["tools"]) == 4
    assert fake.calls[0][2]["headers"]["Authorization"] == "Bearer test-key"
    assert fake.calls[0][1] == "https://ollama.com/api/chat"
    assert [(c.id, c.name, c.arguments) for c in r.tool_calls] == [("call_1", "lookup_kev", {"cve_id": "CVE-2026-69730"})]
    assert r.assistant_message()["tool_calls"][0]["function"]["name"] == "lookup_kev"


def test_string_arguments_and_missing_id(settings, post):
    post(FakeResponse(200, ollama_body(tool_calls=[
        {"function": {"name": "lookup_kev", "arguments": '{"cve_id": "CVE-2026-69730"}'}},
        {"function": {"name": "lookup_kev", "arguments": "{not json"}}])))
    r = OllamaClient(settings).chat([], purpose="plan")
    assert r.tool_calls[0].arguments == {"cve_id": "CVE-2026-69730"} and r.tool_calls[0].id_generated
    assert r.tool_calls[1].arguments == "{not json"  # left raw for the runner to reject


def test_chat_json(settings, post):
    post(FakeResponse(200, ollama_body(content='{"a": 1}')), FakeResponse(200, ollama_body(content="not json")))
    client = OllamaClient(settings)
    _, parsed, err = client.chat_json([], {"type": "object"})
    assert parsed == {"a": 1} and err is None
    _, parsed, err = client.chat_json([], {"type": "object"})
    assert parsed is None and "not valid JSON" in err


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- failures

def test_retry_on_server_error(settings, post):
    fake = post(FakeResponse(503, {"error": "busy"}), FakeResponse(200, ollama_body(content="ok")))
    assert OllamaClient(settings).chat([]).content == "ok" and len(fake.calls) == 2


def test_auth_error_not_retried(settings, post, tmp_path):
    fake = post(FakeResponse(401, {"error": "unauthorized"}))
    client = OllamaClient(settings, tmp_path / "t.jsonl")
    with pytest.raises(LLMError, match="HTTP 401"):
        client.chat([], purpose="plan")
    assert len(fake.calls) == 1
    entry = json.loads((tmp_path / "t.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()[0])
    assert entry["response"] is None and "401" in entry["error"]


def test_network_down_raises_after_retry(settings, post):
    fake = post(requests.ConnectionError("down"), requests.Timeout("slow"))
    with pytest.raises(LLMError, match="2 attempt"):
        OllamaClient(settings).chat([])
    assert len(fake.calls) == 2


def test_missing_key(settings, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(config, "secret", lambda name: None)
    with pytest.raises(LLMError, match="OLLAMA_API_KEY"):
        OllamaClient(settings).chat([])


def test_transcript_has_no_secret(settings, post, tmp_path):
    post(FakeResponse(200, ollama_body(content="ok")))
    OllamaClient(settings, tmp_path / "t.jsonl").chat([{"role": "user", "content": "x"}], purpose="p")
    text = (tmp_path / "t.jsonl").read_text()
    assert "test-key" not in text and '"purpose": "p"' in text


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- fabricated tool output

@pytest.mark.parametrize("text", [
    'lookup_kev(cve_id="CVE-2026-69730") returned not in KEV',
    '{"name": "environment_search", "arguments": {"query_type": "asset", "query": "W01"}}',
    'Result: {"status": "not_found", "in_kev": false}',
    "<tool_call>lookup_vulnerability</tool_call>",
    "Tool result: CVSS 9.8, KEV not listed.",
    '{"call_id": "T9", "records": []}',
])
def test_detects_fabricated_tool_output(text):
    assert detect_fabricated_tool_output(text, TOOLS)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("text", [
    "Evidence gathering complete. T1 and T3 cover the asset and KEV status.",
    "I will look up the vulnerability record next.",
    "",
])
def test_allows_normal_text(text):
    assert detect_fabricated_tool_output(text, TOOLS) == []


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- live

@pytest.mark.live
def test_live_model_makes_a_real_tool_call(tmp_path):
    s = config.load_settings()
    client = OllamaClient(s, tmp_path / "t.jsonl")
    r = client.chat([{"role": "system", "content": "Use tools to gather evidence. Do not answer from memory."},
                     {"role": "user", "content": "Is CVE-2026-69730 in the CISA KEV catalog?"}],
                    tools=tool_specs(s), purpose="live-test")
    assert r.tool_calls, f"model answered without a tool call: {r.content[:200]}"
    call = r.tool_calls[0]
    assert call.name == "lookup_kev"
    validate_arguments(call.name, call.arguments, s)  # raises if the arguments break the contract
    assert detect_fabricated_tool_output(r.content, TOOLS) == []


@pytest.mark.live
def test_live_json_output_follows_schema(tmp_path):
    schema = {"type": "object", "properties": {"cve_id": {"type": "string"}, "severity": {"enum": ["Low", "Medium", "High", "Critical"]}},
              "required": ["cve_id", "severity"]}
    _, parsed, err = OllamaClient(config.load_settings()).chat_json(
        [{"role": "user", "content": "CVE-2026-69730 has CVSS 9.8. Return its ID and severity band."}], schema)
    assert err is None and parsed["cve_id"] == "CVE-2026-69730" and parsed["severity"] == "Critical"

"""Model client tests: request shape, tool-call parsing, retry, transcript, fabricated-output detection."""

import json

import pytest
import requests

import config
import llm
from fakes import FakeNetwork, FakeResponse
from llm import LLMError, OllamaClient, detect_fabricated_tool_output
from tools.registry import tool_specs, validate_arguments

TOOLS = ["environment_search", "lookup_vulnerability", "lookup_kev", "tavily_search"]


@pytest.fixture
def post(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("OLLAMA_API_KEY", "test-key")
    monkeypatch.setattr(llm, "_sleep", lambda s: None)

    def install(*outcomes):
        fake = FakeNetwork(*outcomes)
        monkeypatch.setattr(llm, "_post", lambda url, **kw: fake("POST", url, **kw))
        return fake
    return install


def ollama_body(content="", tool_calls=None):
    msg = {"role": "assistant", "content": content}
    if tool_calls is not None:
        msg["tool_calls"] = tool_calls
    return {"model": "gemma4:31b", "message": msg, "done": True}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- request and parsing

def test_request_shape_and_tool_call_parsing(settings, post, tmp_path):
    fake = post(FakeResponse(200, ollama_body(tool_calls=[
        {"id": "call_1", "function": {"name": "lookup_kev", "arguments": {"cve_id": "CVE-2026-69730"}}}])))
    client = OllamaClient(settings, tmp_path / "t.jsonl")
    r = client.chat([{"role": "user", "content": "hi"}], tools=tool_specs(settings), purpose="plan")
    body = fake.calls[0][2]["json"]
    assert body["options"]["temperature"] == 0 and body["stream"] is False and len(body["tools"]) == 4
    assert fake.calls[0][2]["headers"]["Authorization"] == "Bearer test-key"
    assert fake.calls[0][1] == "https://ollama.com/api/chat"
    assert [(c.id, c.name, c.arguments) for c in r.tool_calls] == [("call_1", "lookup_kev", {"cve_id": "CVE-2026-69730"})]
    assert r.assistant_message()["tool_calls"][0]["function"]["name"] == "lookup_kev"


def test_string_arguments_and_missing_id(settings, post):
    post(FakeResponse(200, ollama_body(tool_calls=[
        {"function": {"name": "lookup_kev", "arguments": '{"cve_id": "CVE-2026-69730"}'}},
        {"function": {"name": "lookup_kev", "arguments": "{not json"}}])))
    r = OllamaClient(settings).chat([], purpose="plan")
    assert r.tool_calls[0].arguments == {"cve_id": "CVE-2026-69730"} and r.tool_calls[0].id_generated
    assert r.tool_calls[1].arguments == "{not json"  # left raw for the runner to reject


def test_chat_json(settings, post):
    post(FakeResponse(200, ollama_body(content='{"a": 1}')), FakeResponse(200, ollama_body(content="not json")))
    client = OllamaClient(settings)
    _, parsed, err = client.chat_json([], {"type": "object"})
    assert parsed == {"a": 1} and err is None
    _, parsed, err = client.chat_json([], {"type": "object"})
    assert parsed is None and "not valid JSON" in err


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- failures

def test_retry_on_server_error(settings, post):
    fake = post(FakeResponse(503, {"error": "busy"}), FakeResponse(200, ollama_body(content="ok")))
    assert OllamaClient(settings).chat([]).content == "ok" and len(fake.calls) == 2


def test_auth_error_not_retried(settings, post, tmp_path):
    fake = post(FakeResponse(401, {"error": "unauthorized"}))
    client = OllamaClient(settings, tmp_path / "t.jsonl")
    with pytest.raises(LLMError, match="HTTP 401"):
        client.chat([], purpose="plan")
    assert len(fake.calls) == 1
    entry = json.loads((tmp_path / "t.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()[0])
    assert entry["response"] is None and "401" in entry["error"]


def test_network_down_raises_after_retry(settings, post):
    fake = post(requests.ConnectionError("down"), requests.Timeout("slow"))
    with pytest.raises(LLMError, match="2 attempt"):
        OllamaClient(settings).chat([])
    assert len(fake.calls) == 2


def test_missing_key(settings, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(config, "secret", lambda name: None)
    with pytest.raises(LLMError, match="OLLAMA_API_KEY"):
        OllamaClient(settings).chat([])


def test_transcript_has_no_secret(settings, post, tmp_path):
    post(FakeResponse(200, ollama_body(content="ok")))
    OllamaClient(settings, tmp_path / "t.jsonl").chat([{"role": "user", "content": "x"}], purpose="p")
    text = (tmp_path / "t.jsonl").read_text()
    assert "test-key" not in text and '"purpose": "p"' in text


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- fabricated tool output

@pytest.mark.parametrize("text", [
    'lookup_kev(cve_id="CVE-2026-69730") returned not in KEV',
    '{"name": "environment_search", "arguments": {"query_type": "asset", "query": "W01"}}',
    'Result: {"status": "not_found", "in_kev": false}',
    "<tool_call>lookup_vulnerability</tool_call>",
    "Tool result: CVSS 9.8, KEV not listed.",
    '{"call_id": "T9", "records": []}',
])
def test_detects_fabricated_tool_output(text):
    assert detect_fabricated_tool_output(text, TOOLS)


@pytest.mark.parametrize("text", [
    "Evidence gathering complete. T1 and T3 cover the asset and KEV status.",
    "I will look up the vulnerability record next.",
    "",
])
def test_allows_normal_text(text):
    assert detect_fabricated_tool_output(text, TOOLS) == []


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- live

@pytest.mark.live
def test_live_model_makes_a_real_tool_call(tmp_path):
    s = config.load_settings()
    client = OllamaClient(s, tmp_path / "t.jsonl")
    r = client.chat([{"role": "system", "content": "Use tools to gather evidence. Do not answer from memory."},
                     {"role": "user", "content": "Is CVE-2026-69730 in the CISA KEV catalog?"}],
                    tools=tool_specs(s), purpose="live-test")
    assert r.tool_calls, f"model answered without a tool call: {r.content[:200]}"
    call = r.tool_calls[0]
    assert call.name == "lookup_kev"
    validate_arguments(call.name, call.arguments, s)  # raises if the arguments break the contract
    assert detect_fabricated_tool_output(r.content, TOOLS) == []


@pytest.mark.live
def test_live_json_output_follows_schema(tmp_path):
    schema = {"type": "object", "properties": {"cve_id": {"type": "string"}, "severity": {"enum": ["Low", "Medium", "High", "Critical"]}},
              "required": ["cve_id", "severity"]}
    _, parsed, err = OllamaClient(config.load_settings()).chat_json(
        [{"role": "user", "content": "CVE-2026-69730 has CVSS 9.8. Return its ID and severity band."}], schema)
    assert err is None and parsed["cve_id"] == "CVE-2026-69730" and parsed["severity"] == "Critical"

content.text:
Step 4 is done and verified. All 108 tests pass (offline and live), and the hand-run round trip worked end to end:

1. The model made two real tool calls (`lookup_kev` and `environment_search "W01"`) through the API's structured `tool_calls` field.
2. The runner executed them as T1 and T2 and kept the model's own call IDs (`call_nyuwajsr`, `call_h8rmhjat`) in the trace.
3. The model read the results and answered citing T1, correctly reporting "not in KEV" and that W01 runs DNS Server.

## What I built

**`src/llm.py`** makes the calls to Ollama Cloud:
- `chat()` sends `gemma4:31b` the tool list at temperature 0. Tool requests are read only from the API's `tool_calls` field.
- Arguments sent as a string are parsed; unparseable ones are passed on unchanged so the runner rejects them as invalid.
- It retries once on server or network errors and fails immediately on an authentication error.
- Every request and reply goes into `model_transcript.jsonl`. A test confirms the API key never appears there.
- `detect_fabricated_tool_output()` flags reply text that imitates a tool call or result: text like `lookup_kev(...)`, tool-call JSON, `"status": "found"`, tool-call markup, or "Tool result:". Ordinary references like "T1 shows…" are allowed.

**Scripted test model** (`ScriptedLLM` in `tests/fakes.py`) stands in for the real one so Step 5 can test the whole workflow offline.

## A finding that changed the design

Ollama Cloud ignores the `format` (JSON schema) field for `gemma4:31b`: it returned prose like "ID: CVE-2026-69730 / Severity Band: Critical". So `chat_json()` now:
- puts the schema in a system instruction (still sending `format` in case the service starts honoring it);
- unwraps code fences if the model adds them;
- **validates the reply against the schema in code**, so a bad reply comes back as a clear error.

With the instruction in the prompt the model returned valid JSON every time. I'll record this in the design-vs-implementation notes.

## Step 5 – Orchestrator (awaiting your approval)

`src/orchestrator.py`, `src/prompts.py` and `src/assemble.py` will implement your workflow table:

1. **Intake (code).**
   - Checks the CVE ID format and that the environment file loads.
   - Creates `runs/<timestamp>/` and copies the inputs and settings into it.
   - If intake fails, it stops with P-RV-F and saves a short failure record.
2. **Plan and follow-up rounds (model, at most 5).**
   - The prompt gives the risk question, the facts the policy needs, and the tool guidance.
   - Any text reply that looks like a fake tool result is rejected, the model is told to use real tool calls, and the rejection uses up a round.
3. **Evidence completeness (code).**
   - Checks that `environment_search` and `lookup_vulnerability` both succeeded.
   - If not, the model gets one prompt to call them; if they still haven't succeeded, the result is P-RV-F.
4. **Fact extraction (model, JSON).**
   - Returns C1–C3, the factor scores, assumptions, unknowns and conflicts.
   - Every fact must cite a call ID and a locator.
5. **Fact validation (code).**
   - Every cited call exists and succeeded.
   - The facts the rating depends on are re-checked against the raw saved outputs of the calls they cite:
     - CVSS vector, KEV status, OS, services and fixed build.
     - RTO against the business-service record.
     - C3 must stay "unknown" while the OS build is null.
     - "Exploitation More Likely" must actually appear in a cited search result.
   - The model gets one retry with the errors listed; if that fails too, the result is P-RV-F.
6. **Gate 1 and Gate 2 (code):** `policy.evaluate()`.
7. **Explanation (model, JSON).** The summary, severity vs local risk, recommended action and confidence explanation. Code ignores any scores in this reply, so the model can't change the rating here.
8. **Assemble and save (code).**
   - Code assigns E1, E2, … and fills each evidence item's source, URL, date and live/cached label from the tool trace.
   - It runs the validator and saves `assessment.json` with the validation results.
   - Analyst review is left as `pending` for Step 6.

**New validator checks:**
- Each trace entry's model call ID appears in the transcript as a structured tool call, and the reverse.
- At least one call was `selected_by: model`.
- Agent-produced assessments must include raw output files.

**Offline tests with the scripted model:**
- The normal run ends in P-IE with provisional P-H-L4I2.
- A fake tool result written as text is rejected and never becomes evidence.
- Citing a call ID that doesn't exist is caught.
- A CVSS vector that differs from the tool output is caught.
- A missing required tool leads to one prompt, then P-RV-F.
- The model service going down mid-run is handled.

"""Prompts and model-output schemas for the three model steps in the design's workflow table.

  1. Plan tool calling / follow-up loop  -> PLAN_SYSTEM, plan_user()
  2. Extract facts and assign scores      -> EXTRACT_SYSTEM, extract_user(), EXTRACTION_SCHEMA
  3. Explain and recommend                -> EXPLAIN_SYSTEM, explain_user(), EXPLANATION_SCHEMA

Plus the corrective messages the orchestrator sends inside the loops (fabricated tool output,
missing required evidence, round cap, failed fact validation).

The model never computes likelihood/impact totals, the matrix result, the rating, the policy rule or
the confidence level; policy.py does. Every run saves prompt_bundle() to runs/<id>/prompts.json.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json

PROMPT_VERSION = "prompts-v1.0"
COMPLETE_SIGNAL = "EVIDENCE GATHERING COMPLETE"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared policy text (from Project_Design.docx, "Rating Policy"). Used by the extraction prompt so
# the model scores the judgment factors with the group's exact definitions.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

APPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS = """\
C1: The asset's OS is in the CVE's affected products list.
C2: The DNS Server service (the vulnerable component) is installed on the asset.
C3: The asset's OS build is below the fixed build for that OS (Windows Server 2022: below 10.0.20348.5622, KB5122882)."""

CONDITION_RESULTS = """\
"true"        - the tool evidence shows the condition holds.
"false"       - the tool evidence explicitly shows it does not hold (e.g. a build at or above the fixed build).

  1. Plan tool calling / follow-up loop  -> PLAN_SYSTEM, plan_user()
  2. Extract facts and assign scores      -> EXTRACT_SYSTEM, extract_user(), EXTRACTION_SCHEMA
  3. Explain and recommend                -> EXPLAIN_SYSTEM, explain_user(), EXPLANATION_SCHEMA

Plus the corrective messages the orchestrator sends inside the loops (fabricated tool output,
missing required evidence, round cap, failed fact validation).

The model never computes likelihood/impact totals, the matrix result, the rating, the policy rule or
the confidence level; policy.py does. Every run saves prompt_bundle() to runs/<id>/prompts.json.
"""

import json

PROMPT_VERSION = "prompts-v1.0"
COMPLETE_SIGNAL = "EVIDENCE GATHERING COMPLETE"

# Shared policy text (from Project_Design.docx, "Rating Policy"). Used by the extraction prompt so
# the model scores the judgment factors with the group's exact definitions.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

APPLICABILITY_CONDITIONS = """\
C1: The asset's OS is in the CVE's affected products list.
C2: The DNS Server service (the vulnerable component) is installed on the asset.
C3: The asset's OS build is below the fixed build for that OS (Windows Server 2022: below 10.0.20348.5622, KB5122882)."""

CONDITION_RESULTS = """\
"true"        - the tool evidence shows the condition holds.
"false"       - the tool evidence explicitly shows it does not hold (e.g. a build at or above the fixed build).
"unknown"     - the evidence needed to decide is missing (e.g. os_build is null). null means unknown, never safe.
"conflicting" - two cited sources disagree on a fact this condition depends on."""

  0 = isolated (no realistic network path)   1 = broad internal access   2 = public-facing / Internet-exposed
  Use null only if the evidence cannot support any score; policy then defaults to 1.

  kev_listed                 - from lookup_kev in_kev.
  credible_in_the_wild       - a vendor, government or known security-vendor report of exploitation in the wild (outside KEV).
  public_poc                 - a credible public proof-of-concept exists.
  vendor_exploitation_likely - the vendor rates exploitation as likely (e.g. Microsoft "Exploitation More Likely").
Asset criticality: 0 = non-critical   1 = business-important   2 = critical
Blast radius:      0 = single host    1 = entire service or department   2 = domain / organization-wide

The prompts are written in [src/prompts.py](src/prompts.py) and ready for your review. Both output schemas are valid JSON Schema, and every run will save all prompts and schemas to `runs/<id>/prompts.json` with the label `prompts-v1.0`.

## What's in the file

**1. Planning (`PLAN_SYSTEM`, `plan_user`).** The model plays the evidence-gathering stage and does not rate.
- **Rules:**
  - Request tools only through the tool-calling interface, and never write tool calls or results as text.
  - Don't answer from memory, and refer to results by their call ID.
  - Treat null as unknown, never safe.
  - Correct a bad request once.
  - At most 5 rounds.
- **Evidence needs, not queries.** It lists 7 things to cover: vulnerability, asset record, scope, reachability, business impact, KEV, and exploit and remediation context. It doesn't say which tool or query covers each, so choosing the tools and writing the queries stays with the model, as the assignment requires.
- **Finishing.** The model signals it's done with `EVIDENCE GATHERING COMPLETE` and one line per item naming the call IDs that cover it. That makes coverage easy to check.
- **The user message** carries the risk question, the CVE, the asset, the environment snapshot and the date.
- **Corrective messages** for a fake tool result, the round limit, and missing required lookups.

**2. Fact extraction (`EXTRACT_SYSTEM`, `EXTRACTION_SCHEMA`).**
- **Citations:** every fact cites `{call_id, locator, fact}`. Only call IDs from this run are allowed, and identifiers (CVSS vector, builds, KBs, RTO) must be copied exactly.
- **Policy text:** includes your C1–C3 definitions, what true / false / unknown / conflicting mean, and your scoring definitions.
- **What the model judges:** only reachability, asset criticality, blast radius, the four exploit-activity yes/no answers, and RTO.
- **What code computes:** exploitability from the CVSS vector, the totals, the matrix, the rule and the confidence.
- **Unknowns:** `decisive=true` only when the answer would change C1–C3, and it must name the condition.
- **Retry:** `FACT_VALIDATION_FAILED` returns the problems code found and asks for the complete corrected JSON. This is the one retry.

**3. Explanation (`EXPLAIN_SYSTEM`, `EXPLANATION_SCHEMA`).** It receives the code-computed decision and the validated facts.
- It must not change any score, and code ignores any it writes anyway.
- It must separate CVSS severity from local risk.
- For Insufficient Evidence it must say the rating isn't binding and give the provisional rating and its condition.
- For Review Needed it must say what failed or conflicted.
- It returns a summary, an explanation of severity vs local risk, a confidence explanation, and an action block. The action block has the next step, priority (Immediate / Urgent / High / Normal / Low), owner, interim measures, and what evidence would change the decision and how.

## Decisions for you

1. **The fixed build is written into the C3 definition.** It reads "below 10.0.20348.5622, KB5122882", matching your design wording. The risk is that the model copies the build from the prompt instead of from the evidence. That would quietly defeat the conflicting-evidence test, where the cached NVD fixed build is changed. I recommend generic wording: *"C3: the asset's OS build is below the fixed build that lookup_vulnerability reports for that OS."* Fact validation still checks the build against the tool output either way. Change it?
2. **Priority options.** Your human JSON used "Urgent". Are Immediate / Urgent / High / Normal / Low the right choices?
3. **Risk question.** I'll store your design's risk question word for word in `config/settings.json` and pass it into the planning message. OK?

Once you've reviewed the file and answered these, I'll build the rest of Step 5: orchestrator, fact validation, assembly, the new validator checks and the scripted end-to-end tests.

"""Orchestration: the design's workflow table, one function per step.

  Intake (code) -> Plan + follow-up loop (model, tools) -> Evidence completeness (code)
  -> Extract facts (model) -> Fact validation (code) -> Gate 1 / Gate 2 (code, policy.py)
  -> Explain and recommend (model) -> Assemble, validate and save (code) -> Analyst review (human, review.py)

Everything a run uses or produces is saved under runs/<run_id>/: config, prompts, input copies with
hashes, raw tool outputs, the model transcript, the run log and the assessment.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
from datetime import datetime
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Callable, Optional

import config
import prompts
from assemble import build_assessment, fallback_explanation
from factcheck import validate_facts
from llm import LLMError, OllamaClient, detect_fabricated_tool_output
from policy import PolicyInputs, evaluate, parse_cvss_vector
from tools.registry import ToolRunner, load_raw_output
from validate import validate_assessment

CVE_RE = re.compile(r"^CVE-\d{4}-\d{4,}$")
REQUIRED_TOOLS = ("environment_search", "lookup_vulnerability")
SUCCESS = ("found", "not_found")
TOOL_MESSAGE_CHARS = 20000


class StopRun(Exception):
    """A step that, per the design, ends the run with Review Needed before an assessment can be built."""

    def __init__(self, stage: str, reason: str):
        super().__init__(f"{stage}: {reason}")
        self.stage, self.reason = stage, reason


def _now() -> str:
    return datetime.now().astimezone().isoformat(timespec="seconds")


def _rel(p: Path) -> str:
    try:
        return p.resolve().relative_to(config.ROOT).as_posix()
    except ValueError:
        return str(p.resolve())


def _sha(p: Path) -> str:
    return hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest()


def _code_version() -> dict:
    try:

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- step 1: intake

def intake(settings: dict, run_dir: Path) -> tuple[dict, dict]:
    """Validate the CVE ID and the environment snapshot; save input copies. Raises StopRun (P-RV-F)."""
    inp = settings["inputs"]
    if not CVE_RE.match(inp["cve_id"] or ""):
        raise StopRun("intake", f"malformed CVE ID {inp['cve_id']!r}")
    env_path = config.path(inp["environment_snapshot"]["path"])
    threat_path = config.path(inp["threat_input"]["path"])
    if not env_path.is_file():
        raise StopRun("intake", f"environment snapshot {inp['environment_snapshot']['path']} not found")
    try:
        env = json.loads(env_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError) as err:
        raise StopRun("intake", f"environment snapshot is not parseable JSON: {err}")
    if not isinstance(env, dict) or not isinstance(env.get("assets"), list):
        raise StopRun("intake", "environment snapshot has no assets list")
    if inp["asset_id"] not in {a.get("asset_id") for a in env["assets"]}:
        raise StopRun("intake", f"asset {inp['asset_id']} is not in the environment snapshot")
    if not threat_path.is_file():
        raise StopRun("intake", f"saved threat input {inp['threat_input']['path']} not found")

    inputs_dir = run_dir / "inputs"
    inputs_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

        "environment_data_type": inp["environment_snapshot"]["data_type"], "environment_path": inp["environment_snapshot"]["path"],
        "run_date": datetime.now().astimezone().date().isoformat(),

def _tool_message(name: str, payload: dict) -> dict:
    content = json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False)
    if len(content) > TOOL_MESSAGE_CHARS:
        content = content[:TOOL_MESSAGE_CHARS] + f' ... [truncated; full result saved as {payload.get("call_id")}]'
    return {"role": "tool", "tool_name": name, "content": content}


class Planner:
    """Runs the model's tool-calling conversation. The model chooses tools and queries; code executes them."""

    def __init__(self, llm, runner: ToolRunner, settings: dict, log: RunLog):
        self.llm, self.runner, self.settings, self.log = llm, runner, settings, log
        self.rounds = 0
        self.fabrications: list[dict] = []
        self.budget_refusals = 0

    def _execute(self, reply) -> None:
        for tc in reply.tool_calls:
            if len(self.runner.trace) >= self.settings["model"]["max_tool_calls"]:
                self.budget_refusals += 1
                payload = {"call_id": None, "tool": tc.name, "status": "failed",
                           "error": "Tool-call budget exhausted; not executed."}
                self.log("tool_budget_refused", tool=tc.name, model_call_id=tc.id)
            else:
                payload = self.runner.execute(tc.name, tc.arguments, model_call_id=tc.id)
                self.log("tool_call", call_id=payload["call_id"], tool=tc.name, arguments=tc.arguments,

        """One model turn. Returns 'tools', 'complete', 'rejected' or 'text'."""

        self.messages.append(reply.assistant_message())
        if reply.tool_calls:
            self._execute(reply)
            return "tools"
        reasons = detect_fabricated_tool_output(reply.content, self.runner.names)
        if reasons:
            self.fabrications.append({"turn": purpose, "reasons": reasons, "content": reply.content[:500]})
            self.log("fabricated_tool_output_rejected", turn=purpose, reasons=reasons)
            self.messages.append({"role": "user", "content": prompts.FABRICATION_REJECTED.format(
                reasons="; ".join(reasons), complete=prompts.COMPLETE_SIGNAL)})
            return "rejected"
        if prompts.COMPLETE_SIGNAL in reply.content.upper():
            self.log("model_signalled_complete", turn=purpose, summary=reply.content[:1500])
            return "complete"
        self.messages.append({"role": "user", "content": f'Request tools through the tool-calling interface, or reply with '
                                                         f'"{prompts.COMPLETE_SIGNAL}" if evidence gathering is finished.'})
        return "text"

    def gather(self, intake_facts: dict) -> None:
        max_rounds = self.settings["model"]["max_tool_rounds"]
        self.messages = [{"role": "system", "content": prompts.plan_system(max_rounds)},
                         {"role": "user", "content": prompts.plan_user(intake_facts)}]
        while self.rounds < max_rounds:
            self.rounds += 1
            if self._turn(f"plan-{self.rounds}") == "complete":
                return
        self.log("round_cap_reached", rounds=self.rounds)

    def missing_required(self) -> list[str]:
        done = {t["tool"] for t in self.runner.trace if t["result_status"] in SUCCESS}
        return [t for t in REQUIRED_TOOLS if t not in done]

    def completeness_followup(self, missing: list[str]) -> None:
        """Design: one loop back to the model when required lookups are missing."""
        self.log("evidence_incomplete", missing=missing)
        self.messages.append({"role": "user", "content": prompts.MISSING_REQUIRED_EVIDENCE.format(
            missing=", ".join(missing), complete=prompts.COMPLETE_SIGNAL)})
        for i in range(2):  # the follow-up tool turn, then its completion reply
            if self._turn(f"completeness-{i + 1}") != "tools":
                break


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- steps 5-6: extract and validate facts

def successful_results(trace: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
    return [{"call_id": t["call_id"], "tool": t["tool"], "arguments": t["arguments"], "result": load_raw_output(t)["result"]}
            for t in trace if t["result_status"] in SUCCESS]


def extract_and_validate(llm, trace, intake_facts, settings, log) -> tuple[dict, dict]:
    """Returns (facts, fact_validation record). Raises StopRun if no usable JSON is produced."""
    messages = [{"role": "system", "content": prompts.EXTRACT_SYSTEM},
                {"role": "user", "content": prompts.extract_user(intake_facts, successful_results(trace))}]
    attempts, problems, facts = [], [], None
    for attempt in (1, 2):
        reply, parsed, err = llm.chat_json(messages, prompts.EXTRACTION_SCHEMA, purpose=f"extract-{attempt}")
        problems = [err] if err else validate_facts(parsed, trace, intake_facts, settings)
        if parsed is not None and not err:
            facts = parsed
        attempts.append({"attempt": attempt, "passed": not problems, "problems": problems})
        log("fact_validation", attempt=attempt, passed=not problems, problems=problems)
        if not problems:
            break
        messages += [{"role": "assistant", "content": reply.content},
                     {"role": "user", "content": prompts.FACT_VALIDATION_FAILED.format(problems="\n".join(f"- {p}" for p in problems))}]
    if facts is None:
        raise StopRun("extract", f"no schema-valid fact extraction after 2 attempts: {problems}")
    return facts, {"passed": not problems, "attempts": attempts}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- step 7: policy

def policy_inputs(facts: dict, trace: list[dict], fact_validation: dict, completeness: dict) -> PolicyInputs:
    f = facts
    vector = f["technical_severity"].get("vector")
    ea = f["likelihood"]["exploit_activity"]
    return PolicyInputs(
        conditions={c["id"]: c["result"] for c in f["conditions"]},
        decisive_tool_failure=bool(completeness["missing"]),
        fact_validation_failed=not fact_validation["passed"],
        any_tool_failed=any(t["result_status"] == "failed" for t in trace),
        assumptions_used=bool(f["assumptions"]),
        reachability=f["likelihood"]["reachability"]["value"],
        cvss_metrics=parse_cvss_vector(vector) if vector else None,
        kev_listed=ea["kev_listed"], credible_in_the_wild=ea["credible_in_the_wild"],
        public_poc=ea["public_poc"], vendor_exploitation_likely=ea["vendor_exploitation_likely"],
        asset_criticality=f["impact"]["asset_criticality"]["value"], blast_radius=f["impact"]["blast_radius"]["value"],
        rto_hours=f["impact"]["rto_hours"]["value"],
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- step 8: explain

def explain(llm, intake_facts, policy_result, facts, log) -> tuple[dict, str]:
    decision_view = {k: policy_result[k] for k in ("decision", "applicability", "gate_2_status", "likelihood", "impact",
                                                   "matrix_result", "confidence")}
    messages = [{"role": "system", "content": prompts.EXPLAIN_SYSTEM},
                {"role": "user", "content": prompts.explain_user(intake_facts, decision_view, facts)}]
    err = None
    for attempt in (1, 2):
        try:
            reply, parsed, err = llm.chat_json(messages, prompts.EXPLANATION_SCHEMA, purpose=f"explain-{attempt}")
        except LLMError as e:
            err = str(e)
            break
        if parsed:
            return parsed, "model"
        messages += [{"role": "assistant", "content": reply.content},
                     {"role": "user", "content": f"Your reply was rejected: {err}. Return the complete JSON object."}]
    log("explanation_failed", error=err)
    return fallback_explanation(policy_result, err), f"fallback ({err})"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the run

def run_assessment(settings: dict, *, llm_factory: Optional[Callable] = None, runs_dir: Optional[Path] = None,
                   run_id: Optional[str] = None) -> dict:
    """Run the full workflow. Returns {"status", "run_dir", "assessment_path" | "failure_path", ...}."""
    run_id = run_id or f"{datetime.now():%Y%m%d-%H%M%S}_{settings['inputs']['cve_id']}_{settings['inputs']['asset_id']}"
    run_dir = Path(runs_dir or config.path(settings["paths"]["runs_dir"])) / run_id
    run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    log = RunLog(run_dir / "run_log.jsonl")
    (run_dir / "config.json").write_text(json.dumps(config.redacted(settings), indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    (run_dir / "prompts.json").write_text(json.dumps(prompts.prompt_bundle(settings["model"]["max_tool_rounds"]), indent=2),
                                          encoding="utf-8")
    transcript = run_dir / "model_transcript.jsonl"
    llm = (llm_factory or (lambda path: OllamaClient(settings, path)))(transcript)
    log("run_started", run_id=run_id, model=settings["model"]["name"],
        fault_injection={k: v for k, v in settings["fault_injection"].items() if not k.startswith("$")})

    stage = "intake"
    planner = None
    try:
        intake_facts, env = intake(settings, run_dir)
        log("intake_ok", **{k: intake_facts[k] for k in ("cve_id", "asset_id", "environment_id")})

        stage = "plan"
        runner = ToolRunner(settings, env, settings["inputs"]["environment_snapshot"]["path"], run_dir / "tool_outputs")
        planner = Planner(llm, runner, settings, log)
        planner.gather(intake_facts)

        stage = "completeness"
        missing = planner.missing_required()
        followed_up = bool(missing)
        if missing:
            planner.completeness_followup(missing)
            missing = planner.missing_required()
        completeness = {"required": list(REQUIRED_TOOLS), "followed_up": followed_up, "missing": missing}
        log("evidence_completeness", **completeness)
        if not runner.trace:
            raise StopRun("completeness", "the model made no tool calls")

        stage = "extract"
        facts, fact_validation = extract_and_validate(llm, runner.trace, intake_facts, settings, log)

        stage = "policy"
        policy_result = evaluate(policy_inputs(facts, runner.trace, fact_validation, completeness))
        log("policy_result", decision=policy_result["decision"], confidence=policy_result["confidence"])

        stage = "explain"
        explanation, explanation_status = explain(llm, intake_facts, policy_result, facts, log)

        stage = "assemble"
        run = {"run_id": run_id, "run_dir": _rel(run_dir), "prompt_version": prompts.PROMPT_VERSION,
               "code_version": _code_version(), "transcript_path": _rel(transcript), "plan_rounds": planner.rounds,
               "fabrication_rejections": planner.fabrications, "rejected_tool_requests": runner.rejected,
               "completeness": completeness, "fact_validation": fact_validation, "explanation_status": explanation_status}
        assessment = build_assessment(run=run, intake=intake_facts, settings=settings, facts=facts,
                                      policy_result=policy_result, explanation=explanation, trace=runner.trace)
        schema = json.loads(config.path(settings["paths"]["schema"]).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        assessment["validation"] = validate_assessment(assessment, schema)
        passed = assessment["validation"]["schema_valid"] and all(c["passed"] for c in assessment["validation"]["checks"])
        out = run_dir / "assessment.json"
        out.write_text(json.dumps(assessment, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        log("assessment_saved", path=_rel(out), validation_passed=passed)
        return {"status": "completed" if passed else "completed_invalid", "run_dir": run_dir, "assessment_path": out,
                "assessment": assessment, "validation_passed": passed}

    except (StopRun, LLMError) as err:
        reason = err.reason if isinstance(err, StopRun) else str(err)
        stage = err.stage if isinstance(err, StopRun) else stage
        failure = {"run_id": run_id, "status": "stopped", "stage": stage, "rating": "Review Needed",
                   "policy_rule_applied": "P-RV-F", "reason": reason, "at": _now(),
                   "tool_trace": planner.runner.trace if planner else [],
                   "note": "Run stopped before an assessment could be assembled (design: intake failure or unrecoverable "
                           "step). Analyst review required."}
        out = run_dir / "run_failure.json"
        out.write_text(json.dumps(failure, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")
        log("run_stopped", stage=stage, reason=reason)
        return {"status": "stopped", "stage": stage, "reason": reason, "run_dir": run_dir, "failure_path": out}

        attempts.append({"attempt": attempt, "passed": not problems, "problems": problems})
        log("fact_validation", attempt=attempt, passed=not problems, problems=problems)
        if not problems:
            break
        messages += [{"role": "assistant", "content": reply.content},
                     {"role": "user", "content": prompts.FACT_VALIDATION_FAILED.format(problems="\n".join(f"- {p}" for p in problems))}]
    if facts is None:
        raise StopRun("extract", f"no schema-valid fact extraction after 2 attempts: {problems}")
    return facts, {"passed": not problems, "attempts": attempts}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- step 7: policy

def policy_inputs(facts: dict, trace: list[dict], fact_validation: dict, completeness: dict) -> PolicyInputs:
    f = facts
    vector = f["technical_severity"].get("vector")
    ea = f["likelihood"]["exploit_activity"]
    return PolicyInputs(
        conditions={c["id"]: c["result"] for c in f["conditions"]},
        decisive_tool_failure=bool(completeness["missing"]),
        fact_validation_failed=not fact_validation["passed"],
        any_tool_failed=any(t["result_status"] == "failed" for t in trace),
        assumptions_used=bool(f["assumptions"]),
        reachability=f["likelihood"]["reachability"]["value"],
        cvss_metrics=parse_cvss_vector(vector) if vector else None,
        kev_listed=ea["kev_listed"], credible_in_the_wild=ea["credible_in_the_wild"],
        public_poc=ea["public_poc"], vendor_exploitation_likely=ea["vendor_exploitation_likely"],
        asset_criticality=f["impact"]["asset_criticality"]["value"], blast_radius=f["impact"]["blast_radius"]["value"],
        rto_hours=f["impact"]["rto_hours"]["value"],
    )


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- step 8: explain

def explain(llm, intake_facts, policy_result, facts, log) -> tuple[dict, str]:
    decision_view = {k: policy_result[k] for k in ("decision", "applicability", "gate_2_status", "likelihood", "impact",
                                                   "matrix_result", "confidence")}
    messages = [{"role": "system", "content": prompts.EXPLAIN_SYSTEM},
                {"role": "user", "content": prompts.explain_user(intake_facts, decision_view, facts)}]
    err = None
    for attempt in (1, 2):
        try:
            reply, parsed, err = llm.chat_json(messages, prompts.EXPLANATION_SCHEMA, purpose=f"explain-{attempt}")
        except LLMError as e:
            err = str(e)
            break
        if parsed:
            return parsed, "model"
        messages += [{"role": "assistant", "content": reply.content},
                     {"role": "user", "content": f"Your reply was rejected: {err}. Return the complete JSON object."}]
    log("explanation_failed", error=err)
    return fallback_explanation(policy_result, err), f"fallback ({err})"


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the run

def run_assessment(settings: dict, *, llm_factory: Optional[Callable] = None, runs_dir: Optional[Path] = None,
                   run_id: Optional[str] = None) -> dict:
    """Run the full workflow. Returns {"status", "run_dir", "assessment_path" | "failure_path", ...}."""
    run_id = run_id or f"{datetime.now():%Y%m%d-%H%M%S}_{settings['inputs']['cve_id']}_{settings['inputs']['asset_id']}"
    run_dir = Path(runs_dir or config.path(settings["paths"]["runs_dir"])) / run_id
    run_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    log = RunLog(run_dir / "run_log.jsonl")
    (run_dir / "config.json").write_text(json.dumps(config.redacted(settings), indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    (run_dir / "prompts.json").write_text(json.dumps(prompts.prompt_bundle(settings["model"]["max_tool_rounds"]), indent=2),
                                          encoding="utf-8")
    transcript = run_dir / "model_transcript.jsonl"
    llm = (llm_factory or (lambda path: OllamaClient(settings, path)))(transcript)
    log("run_started", run_id=run_id, model=settings["model"]["name"],
        fault_injection={k: v for k, v in settings["fault_injection"].items() if not k.startswith("$")})

    stage = "intake"
    planner = None
    try:
        intake_facts, env = intake(settings, run_dir)
        log("intake_ok", **{k: intake_facts[k] for k in ("cve_id", "asset_id", "environment_id")})

        stage = "plan"
        runner = ToolRunner(settings, env, settings["inputs"]["environment_snapshot"]["path"], run_dir / "tool_outputs")
        planner = Planner(llm, runner, settings, log)
        planner.gather(intake_facts)

        stage = "completeness"
        missing = planner.missing_required()
        followed_up = bool(missing)
        if missing:
            planner.completeness_followup(missing)
            missing = planner.missing_required()
        completeness = {"required": list(REQUIRED_TOOLS), "followed_up": followed_up, "missing": missing}
        log("evidence_completeness", **completeness)
        if not runner.trace:
            raise StopRun("completeness", "the model made no tool calls")

        stage = "extract"
        facts, fact_validation = extract_and_validate(llm, runner.trace, intake_facts, settings, log)

        stage = "policy"
        policy_result = evaluate(policy_inputs(facts, runner.trace, fact_validation, completeness))
        log("policy_result", decision=policy_result["decision"], confidence=policy_result["confidence"])

        stage = "explain"
        explanation, explanation_status = explain(llm, intake_facts, policy_result, facts, log)

        stage = "assemble"
        run = {"run_id": run_id, "run_dir": _rel(run_dir), "prompt_version": prompts.PROMPT_VERSION,
               "code_version": _code_version(), "transcript_path": _rel(transcript), "plan_rounds": planner.rounds,
               "fabrication_rejections": planner.fabrications, "rejected_tool_requests": runner.rejected,
               "completeness": completeness, "fact_validation": fact_validation, "explanation_status": explanation_status}
        assessment = build_assessment(run=run, intake=intake_facts, settings=settings, facts=facts,
                                      policy_result=policy_result, explanation=explanation, trace=runner.trace)
        schema = json.loads(config.path(settings["paths"]["schema"]).read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        assessment["validation"] = validate_assessment(assessment, schema)
